akhfash:16-16.t: He said ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافاً﴾: its singular is "اللِّفُّ".

akhfash:26-26.t: And He said ﴿جَزَآءً وِفَاقاً﴾: He means "it matched their deeds in exact accord" (وافَقَ أهْمالَهُم وِفاقا), as you say "قاتَل قِتالا". «[Translator's note: the source writes «أهمالهم»; presumably «أعمالهم», "their deeds".]»

akhfash:28-28.t: And He said ﴿وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً﴾: because its verb has four (letters), He wanted to make it like the pattern "أَفعَلْتُ" — "إِفْعالاً", so He said ﴿كِذَّاباً﴾, making it match the number (of letters) of its maṣdar (verbal noun). On this analogy you say "قاتل" — "قِيتَالا", and it is part of the speech of the Arabs.

akhfash:29-29.t: And He said ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَاباً﴾: He made ﴿كلَّ﴾ accusative even though the verb is occupied with the hāʾ (the pronoun), because what precedes it has had a verb operate on it, so He made it run in the same way and had an implied verb govern it.

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ﴾: if you wish, you make it "he looks (to see) what thing his hands have sent forth" (ينظر أيّ شيء قدّمت يداه), and its description (ṣifa) is "قدمت". And some said: "It is only 'he looks to what his hands have sent forth' (ينظر الى ما قدمت يداه)", and "إلى" ("to") was dropped.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿عَمَّ﴾ about what thing ﴿يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ are some of Quraysh asking one another?

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ an explanation of that thing; the question is to magnify it; it is the Quran which the Prophet ﷺ brought, containing the resurrection and other things,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ the believers affirm it and the unbelievers deny it.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent; ﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ what will befall them for their denial of it.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ emphasis (tawkīd); ثُمَّ was used in it to indicate that the second threat is severer than the first. Then the Exalted pointed to [His] power to resurrect, and said:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا﴾ a bed, like a cradle,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا﴾ by which the earth is made firm, as tents are made firm by pegs; the question is for affirmation (taqrīr).

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا﴾ rest for your bodies,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا﴾ a covering with its darkness,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا﴾ a time for livelihoods,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا﴾ seven heavens ﴿شِدَادًا﴾ plural of شَدِيدَة, i.e. strong and firmly made, unaffected by the passing of time,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا﴾ shining ﴿وَهَّاجًا﴾ blazing, meaning the sun,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ﴾ the clouds whose time to rain has come, like the muʿṣir, the girl who has come close to menstruation, ﴿مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا﴾ pouring,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا﴾ such as wheat ﴿وَنَبَاتًا﴾ such as figs,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ﴾ orchards ﴿أَلْفَافًا﴾ intertwined, plural of لَفِيف, like شَرِيف and أَشْرَاف.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ﴾ between creatures ﴿كَانَ مِيقَاتًا﴾ a time for reward and punishment,

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ the horn; a badal (substitute) for يَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ, or an explanation (bayān) of it; the one who blows is Isrāfīl; ﴿فَتَأْتُونَ﴾ from your graves to the standing place ﴿أَفْوَاجًا﴾ in various groups,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَفُتِّحَتِ السَّمَاءُ﴾ with doubling (tashdīd) and without [وَفُتِحَتْ], is split open for the angels to descend, ﴿فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَابًا﴾ having gates,

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبَالُ﴾ are taken away from their places ﴿فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًا﴾ dust, i.e. like it in the lightness of their movement.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا﴾ lying in wait, or a place of lying in wait,

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿لِلطَّاغِينَ﴾ the unbelievers, so they cannot get past it, ﴿مَآبًا﴾ a place of return for them, so they enter it,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿لَابِثِينَ﴾ an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial, ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. their remaining being decreed, ﴿فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا﴾ ages without end; plural of حُقْب with ḍamma on its first letter.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًا﴾ sleep, for they do not taste it, ﴿وَلَا شَرَابًا﴾ what is drunk for pleasure,

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿حَمِيمًا﴾ water hot to the utmost degree ﴿وَغَسَاقًا﴾ without doubling and with doubling [وَغَسَّاقًا]: what flows from the pus of the people of the Fire; for they do taste it. They are recompensed with that

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا﴾ fitting their deeds: there is no sin greater than unbelief and no punishment greater than the Fire.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا لَا يَرْجُونَ﴾ fear ﴿حِسَابًا﴾ because of their denial of the resurrection,

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ of deeds ﴿أَحْصَيْنَاهُ﴾ We have recorded precisely ﴿كِتَابًا﴾ in writing, in the Preserved Tablet, so that We may recompense it; and among that is their denial of the Quran.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾ i.e. it will be said to them in the Hereafter when the punishment befalls them: taste your recompense; ﴿فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذَابًا﴾ on top of your punishment.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا﴾ a place of triumph in Paradise:

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿حَدَائِقَ﴾ orchards; a badal (substitute) for مَفَازًا, or an explanation (bayān) of it; ﴿وَأَعْنَابًا﴾ conjoined to مَفَازًا,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَكَوَاعِبَ﴾ maidens with rounded breasts, plural of كَاعِب, ﴿أَتْرَابًا﴾ of one age, plural of تِرْب with kasra on the tāʾ and sukūn on the rāʾ,

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا﴾ wine filling its vessels; and in [Sūrat] al-Qitāl: {وَأَنْهَارٌ مِنْ خَمْرٍ}.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا﴾ i.e. in Paradise, when drinking wine and in other states, ﴿لَغْوًا﴾ vain talk ﴿وَلَا كِذَابًا﴾ without doubling, i.e. lying, and with doubling [كِذَّابًا], i.e. one person calling another a liar, unlike what happens in this world when wine is drunk,

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿جَزَاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ i.e. Allah has recompensed them with that as a recompense, ﴿عَطَاءً﴾ a badal (substitute) for جَزَاءً, ﴿حِسَابًا﴾ i.e. abundant, from their saying "He gave to me and aḥsabanī", i.e. gave me so much that I said: enough (ḥasbī)!

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ in the genitive and in the nominative ﴿وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ likewise, and also in the nominative with رَبِّ in the genitive; ﴿لَا يَمْلِكُونَ﴾ i.e. creation ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ the Exalted ﴿خِطَابًا﴾ i.e. no one is able to address Him, out of fear of Him,

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) for لَا يَمْلِكُونَ ﴿يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ﴾ Gabriel, or Allah's army, ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ صَفًّا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. ranged in rows; ﴿لَا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ﴾ i.e. creation, ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ to speak ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ a saying ﴿صَوَابًا﴾ of the believers and the angels, such as interceding for one He is pleased with.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَقُّ﴾ whose occurrence is established, and it is the Day of Resurrection; ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ مَآبًا﴾ a place of return, i.e. returned to Allah through obeying Him, so as to be safe from the punishment on it.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْذَرْنَاكُمْ﴾ O unbelievers of Mecca ﴿عَذَابًا قَرِيبًا﴾ the punishment of the Day of Resurrection that is coming, and everything coming is near; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) for عَذَابًا with its adjective; ﴿يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ﴾ every person ﴿مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ﴾ of good and evil, ﴿وَيَقُولُ الْكَافِرُ يَا﴾ a particle of alerting (ḥarf tanbīh) ﴿لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرَابًا﴾ meaning: so that I would not be punished. He says that when Allah the Exalted says to the beasts, after retaliation has been taken for some of them against others: "Become dust!"

daas-irab:1-5.t: ﴿عَمَّ﴾: composed of ﴿عن﴾, a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾, interrogative, in the position of a genitive by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿عَنِ النَّبَإِ﴾: attached to an omitted verb; ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second adjective; ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿فِيهِ﴾: attached to the khabar (predicate) ﴿مُخْتَلِفُونَ﴾; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its agent; the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying. The verse after it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:6-11.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مِهاداً﴾: second direct object; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالْجِبالَ أَوْتاداً﴾: both conjoined to الأرض مهادا. ﴿وَخَلَقْناكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its agent and its object; ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿نَوْمَكُمْ﴾: first direct object; ﴿سُباتاً﴾: second direct object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً﴾ and ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهارَ مَعاشاً﴾: both conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:12-16.t: ﴿وَبَنَيْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فَوْقَكُمْ﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿سَبْعاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿شِداداً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, and the one following it is conjoined to it. ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ماءً﴾: direct object; ﴿ثَجَّاجاً﴾: adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِنُخْرِجَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزلنا; ﴿بِهِ﴾: attached to نخرج; ﴿حَبًّا﴾: direct object; ﴿وَنَباتاً﴾: conjoined to حبا; ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَلْفافاً﴾: adjective.

daas-irab:17-20.t: ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ﴾: inna and its noun, which is muḍāf to الفصل; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِيقاتاً﴾: its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن… is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: badal (substitute) for يوم الفصل; ﴿يُنْفَخُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent; ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَتَأْتُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿أَفْواجاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَفُتِحَتِ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾: deputy agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَكانَتْ﴾: kāna, its noun being latent; ﴿أَبْواباً﴾: its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. The verse following it is conjoined to it and its i'rab is like it.

daas-irab:21-26.t: ﴿إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كانَتْ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِرْصاداً﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِلطَّاغِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) مرصادا; ﴿مَآباً﴾: a second khabar of كانت. ﴿لابِثِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to what precedes them; ﴿أَحْقاباً﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَذُوقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿بَرْداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَلا شَراباً﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿حَمِيماً﴾: badal (substitute) for شرابا; ﴿غَسَّاقاً﴾: conjoined to حميما. ﴿جَزاءً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿وِفاقاً﴾: naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:27-30.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَرْجُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿حِساباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, the clause كانوا is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl). ﴿وَكَذَّبُوا﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿كِذَّاباً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿كُلَّ﴾: accusative by ishtighāl (a noun governed by an omitted verb that the following verb explains); ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿أَحْصَيْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its agent and its object; ﴿كِتاباً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause explains the omitted one, and the omitted clause is parenthetical. ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of reason; ﴿نَزِيدَكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, its agent latent (mustatir), and the kāf is the first direct object; ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿عَذاباً﴾: second direct object; the verbal clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:31-36.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿مَفازاً﴾: its postponed noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿حَدائِقَ﴾: badal (substitute) for مفازا; ﴿أَعْناباً﴾: conjoined to حدائق; ﴿وَكَواعِبَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَتْراباً﴾: naʿt (adjective) of كواعب; ﴿وَكَأْساً دِهاقاً﴾: both conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿لَغْواً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿لا﴾ is negative; ﴿كِذَّاباً﴾: conjoined to لغوا; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿جَزاءً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: attached to جزاء; ﴿عَطاءً﴾: badal for جزاء; ﴿حِساباً﴾: adjective of عطاء.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿رَبِّ السَّماواتِ﴾: badal (substitute) for ربك, muḍāf to السموات; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined to السموات; ﴿وَما﴾: conjoined to السموات; ﴿بَيْنَهُمَا﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾: badal for رب. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَمْلِكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿مِنْهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿خِطاباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ﴾: an adverb of time, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿وَالْمَلائِكَةُ﴾: conjoined to الروح; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿صَفًّا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَتَكَلَّمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مَنْ﴾: badal (substitute) for the wāw in يتكلمون; ﴿أَذِنَ﴾: a past verb; ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾: agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿وَقالَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿صَواباً﴾: naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْيَوْمُ﴾: its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of اليوم; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and ﴿من﴾ is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿اتَّخَذَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿إِلى رَبِّهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) ﴿مَآباً﴾; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position, and the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.

daas-irab:40-40.t:
[Translator's note: the Arabic source text of this entry is garbled (the opening letters of most quoted words and their brackets are lost, e.g. «ِنَّا»», «وَذاباً»», «وا»»); the quoted words are restored below from the verse (إِنَّا أَنْذَرْناكُمْ عَذاباً قَرِيباً يَوْمَ يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ وَيَقُولُ الْكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُراباً) and the analysis is translated as written.]
﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿أَنْذَرْناكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object; ﴿عَذاباً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿قَرِيباً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَنْظُرُ﴾: an imperfect verb; ﴿الْمَرْءُ﴾: its agent; ﴿ما﴾: direct object; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَيَقُولُ الْكافِرُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يا﴾: a particle drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿لَيْتَنِي﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿كُنْتُ﴾: kāna and its noun; ﴿تُراباً﴾: its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of layta, and the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

dervis-irab:1-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُباتاً) Rest for your bodies. In al-Mukhtār: «al-subāt is sleep, and its origin is rest; from it is His saying, the Exalted: وجعلنا نومكم سباتا; and its pattern is naṣara.» In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«al-subāt, with ḍamma, like ghurāb: heavy sleep, and its origin is rest. From it one says sabata, yasbutu, of the pattern of qatala; and subita, in the passive: he fainted, and also: he died.» Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «سباتا: death; and al-masbūt is the dead, from al-sabt, which is cutting, because he is cut off from movement; and sleep is one of the two takings of the soul (al-tawaffiyayn); and it is on the pattern of the names of diseases.» As for Abū Ḥayyān, he said: «al-subāt is a known illness in which silence overcomes a person excessively until it becomes fatal.»
(الْمُعْصِراتِ) al-muʿṣir: al-Farrāʾ said: the clouds that bring rain but have not yet gathered, like the girl who is muʿṣir, who is about to menstruate but has not yet menstruated. Ibn Qutayba said something similar. And Abū al-Najm al-ʿIjlī said:
تمشي الهوينى مائلا خمارها ... قد أعصرت أو قد دنا إعصارها
(She walks gently, her veil leaning; she has come of age, or her coming of age has drawn near.)
And ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
فكان مجني دون من كنت أتقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I feared was three figures: two full-breasted maidens and a girl come of age.)
(ثَجَّاجاً) al-thajj: pouring down with abundance and force. In the ḥadīth: «The deed most beloved to Allah is al-ʿajj and al-thajj»; al-ʿajj is raising the voice in the talbiya and al-thajj is shedding the blood of the sacrificial animals. One says: the water thajja by itself, i.e. it poured down; and I thajajtuhu, i.e. I poured it, thajjan and thujūjan; so it is intransitive and transitive. [Translator's note: the opening quotation mark before «أحب العمل» is not closed in the source.] In al-Mukhtār: «The water and the blood thajja: flowed, and its pattern is radda; and a thajjāj rain, i.e. pouring down greatly. And al-thajj is also the flowing of the blood of sacrificial animals, and it is intransitive; you say from it: the blood thajja, yathijju (with kasra), thajjan (with fatḥa). I say: al-Azharī transmitted the like of this from Abū ʿUbayda.»
(أَلْفافاً) Intertwined. In al-Asās: «He wrapped (laffa) the garment and other things, and wrapped the thing in his garment, and laffafahu; and he wrapped his head in his clothes, and iltaffa in his clothes, and talaffafa; and the plants became intertwined (iltaffa), and in the land there are talāfīf of herbage; and جنات ألفافا: intertwined; and in it there is a thicket (lafaf) of trees. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
ولقد عرتني منك جدوى أنبتت ... خضرا إلى لفف من الأشجار
(A gift from you came to me that made green things grow, up to a thicket of trees.)
And a man is alaff and a woman laffāʾ; she laffat, talaffu, lafafan, which is the closeness of the thighs from fatness; it is a defect in a man and a praise in a woman. Naṣr ibn Sayyār, ruler of Khurāsān, said:
ولو كنت القتيل وكان حيّا ... تشمّر لا ألفّ ولا سؤوم
(Had I been the slain and he alive, he would have girded himself, neither heavy-thighed nor weary.)
And he said, describing women:
عراض القطا ملتفة ربلاتها ... وما اللفّ أفخاذا بتاركة عقلا»
(Broad of rump, their inner thighs fleshy; and the full-thighed ones do not leave a mind (intact).)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «ألفافا: intertwined; it has no singular, and it is said the singular is liff, with kasra on the lām», so it would be like sirr and asrār. And it is said it is the plural of lafīf — al-Kisāʾī said that — and similar are sharīf and ashrāf, shahīd and ashhād.

* I'rab:
(عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ، عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ، الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ) عن is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun, genitive (majrūr) by عن. It has preceded that the alif of interrogative ما is mostly omitted when a preposition enters upon it. And عمّا was read with the alif retained, and it has preceded that this is permissible by poetic necessity or in a small portion of speech; on this is the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
على ما قام يشتمني لئيم ... كخنزير تمرغ في رماد
(For what reason did a base man rise to revile me, like a swine rolling in ashes?)
What appears is that عمّ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتساءلون, and the interrogative is for magnifying the matter, as if He said: about what thing are they asking one another? Similar is the like of the saying «Zayd — what is Zayd!»: you have made him, because he has no peer, as though he were something hidden from you, so you ask about his kind and examine his essence and substance; you say: what is the ghoul, and what is the ʿanqāʾ? meaning: what thing among things is this? Then it was stripped down to express magnification, until it occurred in the speech of Allah the Exalted, from whom nothing hidden is hidden. وعن النبإ العظيم is a resumed statement presented to clarify that thing, so it is attached to an omitted verb indicated by يتساءلون; it is not a complement of يتساءلون because عمّ is its complement; i.e. they are asking one another about the great news; so it is a grammatical ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). الذي is a second naʿt (adjective) of النبإ; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); فيه is attached to مختلفون, and مختلفون is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. (كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ) A deterrent and threat to those asking in mockery; it contains the sense of threat and menace: the deterrence with the word كلا and the threat with the word سيعلمون. The object of سيعلمون is omitted, its implied form being «what will befall them». ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, and كلا سيعلمون is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of the preceding clause, and the intervention of the conjunction does no harm. The grammarians insist that it can only be a conjunction, even if it conveys emphasis; and it can be answered that there is a noticeable difference, namely that the second threat is more severe than the first; by this consideration it became different from what precedes it, and therefore it was conjoined with ثم. (أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهاداً وَالْجِبالَ أَوْتاداً) A resumed statement presented to set out His power, Glorified is He, to resurrect and to bring proofs of it; He mentioned nine of them. The point in them is that if He is able to do these things, then by plain intuition He is able to resurrect. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), i.e. «We made the earth a resting place». لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; نجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «We»; الأرض is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and مهادا the second direct object, because جعل means transformation (taṣyīr). It may also mean creation, so that مهادا is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). والجبال أوتادا is conjoined to الأرض مهادا. (وَخَلَقْناكُمْ أَزْواجاً) Conjoined to what preceded. خلقناكم is a verb, its agent and its direct object; أزواجا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. of the same kind and resembling one another, males and females. (وَجَعَلْنا نَوْمَكُمْ سُباتاً) Also conjoined. جعلنا is a past verb and its agent; نومكم is the first object of جعلنا and سباتا the second object of جعلنا. (وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً) Also conjoined, and the clause is like the one before it in parsing. (وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهارَ مَعاشاً) Also conjoined, and it too is like the one before it. معاشا is a mīm-maṣdar meaning livelihood, and here it has occurred as an adverb of time, i.e. a time of livelihood. (وَبَنَيْنا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعاً شِداداً)
Also conjoined. بنينا is a past verb and its agent; فوقكم is an adverb attached to بنينا; سبعا is the direct object, i.e. seven heavens; and شدادا is an adjective. (وَجَعَلْنا سِراجاً وَهَّاجاً) Also conjoined. سراجا is the object of جعلنا and وهاجا an adjective; جعل here means creation. (وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ ماءً ثَجَّاجاً) Also conjoined. أنزلنا is a verb and its agent; من المعصرات is attached to أنزلنا; ماء is the direct object and ثجاجا an adjective. (لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَباتاً) The lām is the lām of causation; نخرج is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and it is also attached to أنزلنا. به is attached to نخرج; حبا is the object of نخرج, and نباتا is conjoined to حبا. (وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفافاً) Conjoined to حبا, and the sign of its accusative is the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; ألفافا is an adjective of جنان [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has جنات], i.e. intertwined orchards.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وجعلنا الليل لباسا» there is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh). The point of resemblance is covering, because each of the garment and the night covers the one who wears it; i.e. it conceals you from eyes when you want to save yourselves from an enemy pursuing you, or as a night raid on him when you want to inflict a blow on him far from eyes, or it helps you hide what you do not wish anyone to see. Abū al-Ṭayyib (al-Mutanabbī) glanced at this lofty heaven, as is his custom, and said:
وكم لظلام الليل عندك من يد ... تخبر أن المانوية تكذب
(How many a favour has the darkness of night done for you, showing that the Manichaeans lie!)
وقال رد الأعداء تسري إليهم ... وزارك فيه ذو الدلال المحجب
(It guarded you against the enemies' ruin as you marched by night to them, and in it the coy, veiled beloved visited you.) [Translator's note: the first hemistich is printed garbled in the source; the gloss follows its evident sense.]
The Manichaeans (al-Mānawiyya) are named after Mani, founder of the Manichaean doctrine of two principles in existence, a principle of good and a principle of evil: light and darkness. Mani entered into Persian painting, arranged Chinese painting and drew angels and devils, and he died in 276 CE. The explanation of the Manichaean question is that they said: you find in the world much good and much evil, and one being cannot be both good and evil; so each of good and evil has an independent agent. They said the agent of good is light and the agent of evil is darkness, and they believed that the two are eternal bodies, sentient, hearing and seeing — and all of that is manifestly false.
Abū al-Ṭayyib also said, clinging to the fringes of this lofty eloquence:
أزورهم وسواد الليل يشفع لي ... وأنثني وبياض الصبح يغري
(I visit them while the blackness of night intercedes for me, and I turn back while the whiteness of dawn incites against me.)
And Ibn Zaydūn said:
سرّان في خاطر الظلماء يكتمان ... حتى يكاد لسان الصبح يغشينا
(Two secrets kept hidden in the mind of the darkness, until the tongue of dawn almost reveals us.)

dervis-irab:17-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَراباً) al-sarāb (mirage): what is seen at midday from the intensity of the heat, as though it were water in which houses, trees and other things are reflected. It is proverbial for falsehood and deception; one says «he is more deceptive than a mirage». It means that they (the mountains) become a thing like nothing, because of the dispersal of their parts and the scattering of their substances, as in His saying, the Exalted: «فانت هباء منبثا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads فكانت هباء منبثا]. More of its meaning will come in the section on rhetoric.
(أَحْقاباً) The plural of ḥuqb (with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ), and it is also pluralized as aḥqub:
eighty years or more; and an age; and a year or years. More on what is meant by it will come in the section on i'rab.
(بَرْداً) al-bard is the touch of cold air, i.e. nothing of it touches them that they would find pleasant or that would relieve them of the day's heat. Abū ʿUbayda, al-Kisāʾī, al-Faḍl ibn Khālid and Muʿādh the grammarian said that al-bard here is sleep, and the Arabs call it so because it cools the violence of thirst; among their sayings is «the cold prevented sleep (manaʿa al-bardu al-barda)». The poet said:
فلو شئت حرّمت النساء سواكم ... وإن شئت لم أطعم نقّاخا ولا بردا
(If I wished, I would forbid myself women other than you; and if I wished, I would taste neither cool water nor sleep.)
al-nuqākh is cold water and al-bard is sleep. In the book al-Lughāt fī al-Qurʾān, al-bard is sleep in the dialect of Hudhayl. The lexicons have cited al-bard in the sense of sleep, but its occurrence with this meaning in the verse is strained. What is correct is what the majority said: that al-bard is cold drink, and it suits the word «tasting». From it is the saying:
أماني من سعدى حسان كأنما ... سقتك بها سعدى على ظمأ بردا
منى إن تكن حقا تكن أحسن المنى ... وإلّا فقد عشنا بها زمنا رغدا
(Fair hopes from Suʿdā, as though Suʿdā had given you with them a cool drink upon thirst; hopes which, if true, are the finest of hopes, and if not, we have lived by them a pleasant time.)
On this view the tasting is literal, not figurative.
(غَسَّاقاً) It was read light and with doubling. Its mention has preceded, and that it is the pus that flows from the people of the Fire.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كانَ مِيقاتاً) A resumed statement presented to answer a question that might arise after Allah established the resurrection with the preceding proofs, namely: what is the time of the resurrection? So He said: إن يوم etc. إنّ and its noun; the clause كان is its khabar (predicate); the noun of كان is latent (mustatir), implied as «it», and ميقاتا is its predicate. (يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْواجاً) يوم is a badal (substitute) of يوم الفصل. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a substitute of ميقاتا, or accusative by an omitted verb, implied as «I mean». The clause ينفخ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. ينفخ [Translator's note: the source prints «نفخ»] is an imperfect verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, implied as «he», referring to Isrāfīl, who blows into the Trumpet. فتأتون is conjoined to ينفخ, and أفواجا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw. (وَفُتِحَتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ أَبْواباً) Conjoined to فتأتون. He turned from the imperfect to the past only because of the certainty of its occurrence [Translator's note: the source says «from the past to the imperfect», evidently reversed]. It is said the wāw is circumstantial and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. you come, the state being that the sky has been opened. السماء is the deputy agent; فكانت is conjoined to فتحت; the noun of كان is latent, implied as «it», and أبوابا is its predicate. فتّحت was also read with doubling. (وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ فَكانَتْ سَراباً) Also conjoined. سيّرت is a past verb, passive, and الجبال is the deputy agent; فكانت is conjoined to سيّرت, and سرابا is the predicate of كانت. (إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كانَتْ مِرْصاداً) A resumed statement presented to begin describing the terrors of Jahannam, after He finished describing the general conditions of the Day of Resurrection. إنّ and its noun; the clause كانت is its predicate; the noun of كانت is latent, implied as «it», i.e. Jahannam; and مرصادا is the predicate of كانت, i.e. lying in wait for those punished in it, watching for them; or prepared, in the sense of made ready for them. So it is either from the three-letter raṣada, meaning to watch for, or from the four-letter arṣada, i.e. to prepare. al-mirṣād in the lexicons is the road and the passage. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: al-mirṣād is the boundary at which the watching takes place. (لِلطَّاغِينَ مَآباً) للطاغين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) مرصادا [Translator's note: so in the source; given the closing sentence, «attached to مآبا» was probably meant here], and مآبا is a second predicate of كانت, i.e. a place of return for them and a destination to which they return and go back. And it is permissible to attach للطاغين to مرصاد. (لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً) لابثين is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) of the pronoun concealed in للطاغين, and أحقابا is an adverb attached to لابثين. If it is said: the aḥqāb, however long they extend and however much time is prolonged with them, are finite in any case, whereas the punishment of the disbelievers is not finite [Translator's note: the source prints «متناد», a misprint for «متناه»] — several answers have been given to this question, among them:
1- What is narrated from al-Ḥasan; he said: «Allah the Exalted has not set a term for the people of the Fire; rather He said لابثين فيها أحقابا, and by Allah, it is only that whenever one ḥuqb passes another ḥuqb enters, forever; and the aḥqāb have no term except eternity.» 2- The word aḥqāb does not indicate an end; a single ḥuqb is finite, and the meaning is that they remain in it for aḥqāb in which they taste neither coolness nor drink except scalding water and pus; so the time limit is for the kinds of punishment, not a time limit for remaining and staying. (لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً وَلا شَراباً) The clause لا يذوقون is a ḥāl of the pronoun in لابثين, i.e. remaining without tasting, so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila); or an adjective of أحقابا; and it is said it is resumed. لا is negative; يذوقون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); فيها is attached to يذوقون; بردا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and شرابا is conjoined to بردا. (إِلَّا حَمِيماً وَغَسَّاقاً) إلا is a particle of restriction, and حميما is a substitute of شرابا because the statement is non-affirmative, and غساقا is conjoined to it. This is easier than the path the exegetes took: some of them said it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and al-Kashshāf followed this; he said: «They taste in it no coolness that relieves them of the heat of the Fire and no drink that calms their thirst, but they taste in it scalding water», and al-Jalāl followed him. Abū Ḥayyān said: «What appears is that it is connected, from His saying ولا شرابا.» (جَزاءً وِفاقاً) جزاء is a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. they were recompensed with that as a recompense; and وفاقا is an adjective of جزاء; so the clause is resumed. (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ حِساباً) The clause is a causal explanation of His saying جزاء. إنّ and its noun; the clause كانوا is the predicate of إنهم; كان and its noun, and the clause لا يرجون its predicate; حسابا is the object of يرجون, i.e. a reckoning. (وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كِذَّاباً) The wāw is a conjunction; كذبوا is a verb and its agent; بآياتنا is attached to كذبوا; and كذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. a denying. The pattern fiʿʿāl for faʿʿala is all widespread in the speech of the eloquent Arabs; they hardly say anything else. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «One of them heard me explaining a verse and said: you have explained it with an explaining (fissāran) the like of which has not been heard. And it was read light, being the maṣdar of kadhaba, as evidenced by the saying:
فصدقتها وكذّبتها ... والمرء ينفعه كذابه»
(I told her the truth and I lied to her; and a man's lying benefits him.)
(وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْناهُ كِتاباً) The wāw is a conjunction; كل شيء is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), i.e. «and We counted everything; We counted it». This clause is parenthetical between the cause and its effect, for His coming saying فذوقوا is caused by their denial; and the benefit of the parenthesis is the confirmation of what He asserted in His saying جزاء وفاقا. The clause أحصيناه is explicative, with no grammatical position; أحصيناه is a past verb, its agent and its direct object. كتابا may be a maṣdar from the meaning of أحصيناه, i.e. a counting, with أحصيناه in the sense of «We wrote», because counting and writing meet in the meaning of recording and securing; or it is a maṣdar of أحصينا [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «a maṣdar of an implied كتبنا» is meant]; and it may be a ḥāl in the sense of «written». (فَذُوقُوا فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذاباً) The fāʾ is causal because it is — as we said — caused by their disbelief in the reckoning and their denial of the signs. ذوقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the meaning of the command is humiliation and contempt. The fāʾ is a conjunction; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and future; نزيدكم is an imperfect verb, accusative by لن, and the kāf is the first direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction, and عذابا is the second direct object. (إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفازاً) A resumed statement presented to set out the states of the people of Paradise. للمتقين is the fronted predicate of إنّ and مفازا the delayed noun of إنّ. al-mafāz is a mīm-maṣdar or a noun of place for the place of triumph. In al-Mukhtār: «al-fawz is salvation and attaining good, and it is also perishing; and the pattern of both is qāla.» On this basis, calling the waterless desert mafāza is literal, because it is a place of perishing, since among the meanings of al-fawz is perishing, as you have seen. In al-Qāmūs: «al-fawz: salvation, attaining good, and perishing — a contronym. fāza: he died; and fāza bihi: he attained it; and fāza minhu: he escaped it.» (حَدائِقَ وَأَعْناباً وَكَواعِبَ أَتْراباً وَكَأْساً دِهاقاً) حدائق is the plural of ḥadīqa, which is the round plot of land with palms and water; it is a part-for-whole substitute (badal baʿḍ min kull) of مفازا. أعنابا and what follows it are conjoined to حدائق, and there is no sense in conjoining them to مفازا on the argument that they were mentioned after the gardens to extol their status, for that is far from the ease of the Qurʾān and the absence of forced language in it. (لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْواً وَلا كِذَّاباً) The clause is a ḥāl of المتقين. لا is negative; يسمعون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the agent; فيها is attached to يسمعون; لغوا is the direct object and ولا كذابا is conjoined to لغوا. (جَزاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ عَطاءً حِساباً) جزاء is an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. Allah recompensed them with that as a recompense; من ربك is an adjective of جزاء; and عطاء is a substitute of جزاء. In this substitution there is a subtle secret, namely the hint that this is a favour and a gift, while recompense is based on deserving. Al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as accusative by جزاء as its direct object, i.e. He recompensed them with a gift. حسابا is an adjective of عطاء, meaning «sufficient»; so it is a maṣdar put in place of the adjective, or it remains a maṣdar for intensiveness. (رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُمَا الرَّحْمنِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطاباً) رب in the genitive as a substitute of ربك; and it was read in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. He is the Lord. ما is conjoined to السموات والأرض; بينهما is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما. الرحمن is also a substitute or adjective of رب. The clause لا يملكون is resumed; منه is attached to يملكون, and خطابا is the object. الرحمن was also read in the nominative, so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause لا يملكون its predicate. (يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ وَقالَ صَواباً) يوم is an adverb attached to لا يملكون or to لا يتكلمون; the clause يقوم الروح والملائكة is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; صفا is a ḥāl, i.e. standing in rows. The clause لا يتكلمون is an emphasis of His saying لا يملكون, or resumed. إلا is a particle of restriction; من is a substitute of the wāw in يتكلمون, or accusative by exception because the statement is non-affirmative. The clause أذن is the ṣila of من; له is attached to أذن, and الرحمن is the agent. قال is a past verb, its agent latent, implied as «he», and صوابا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. a correct saying. (ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَقُّ فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ مَآباً) ذلك is the subject, اليوم a substitute and الحق the predicate of ذلك; you may also make اليوم the predicate and الحق an adjective of the predicate. فمن: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it discloses an omitted condition, as if it were said: and since the matter is of this standing, and as mentioned regarding the certainty of the said day, then whoever.... من is conditional, a subject; شاء is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the object of the willing is omitted; اتخذ is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the predicate of من. إلى ربه is attached to مآبا, and مآبا is the object of اتخذ. [Translator's note: in the source the following verse heading is fused into this line; it is separated here.] (إِنَّا أَنْذَرْناكُمْ عَذاباً قَرِيباً)
إنّ and its noun; the clause أنذرناكم is its predicate. أنذرناكم is
a verb, its agent and its first direct object; عذابا is the second direct object and قريبا an adjective. [Translator's note: here too the next verse heading is fused into the text in the source.] (يَوْمَ يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ وَيَقُولُ الْكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُراباً)
يوم is an adverb attached to عذابا; the clause ينظر المرء is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; ما is the direct object, and the clause قدّمت يداه is the ṣila of ما. ويقول الكافر is conjoined to ينظر المرء; you may also make it resumed or circumstantial. يا is a particle of alerting, or the one addressed is omitted; ليتني: ليت and its noun; the clause كنت is its predicate, and ترابا is the predicate of كنت.

* Rhetoric:
Simile (tashbīh) is frequent in this sūra, and we point here to His saying «وسيّرت الجبال فكانت سرابا». It is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh) from which the particle has been omitted, and the point of resemblance has also been omitted, namely that what is seen is contrary to reality. Just as the mirage is seen from afar by the parched, burning-thirsty man as though it were water, so he rejoices at it and hurries to it, until when he reaches it after long weariness he finds it to be nothing — likewise the mountains are seen as if they were mountains, and they are not so in actual fact.

farraa:1-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾.
It is said: About what thing are they asking one another? — meaning Quraysh. Then He said to His Prophet ﷺ: they are asking one another about the great news, meaning the Qur'an. It is also said: about what Quraysh are talking regarding the Qur'an. Then He answered, so that عم يتساءلون became as though [in the meaning of]: for what reason are they asking one another about the Qur'an? Then He informed and said: ﴿ٱلَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ — between one who affirms it and one who denies it; that is their disagreement. The readers agreed on the yāʾ in His saying: ﴿كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾. Al-Ḥasan alone read: "كلا ستعلمون", and that is correct. It is like His saying — even though there is no "say" before it [here] —: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾ and سَيُغْلَبُون.
His saying: ﴿ثَجَّاجاً﴾: like the mouths of water-skins (العزالي): [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here.]

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَفُتِحَتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَاباً﴾.
Like: ﴿إِذَا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ and ﴿وإذا السماءُ فُرِجَتْ﴾; the meaning is one, and Allah knows best. That is how the exegesis has come.

farraa:23-23.t:
[123/a] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّبِثِينَ فِيهَآ أَحْقَاباً﴾.
I was told from al-Aʿmash that he said: It reached us from ʿAlqama that he read "لَبِثين", and that is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullāh. People since then read (لابثين), and it is the better of the two, because (لابثين), when it is in a position where it acts and puts [something] in the accusative, has the alif, like: الطامع (the one who covets) and الباخل (the one who withholds) shortly. اللَّبِث is the slow one, and it is permissible, as one says: رجل طمِعٌ and طامع (a covetous man). If you said: هذا طمِعٌ فيما قِبَلك (this one covets what you have), it would be permissible. Labīd said:
أوْ مِسْحَلٌ عَملٌ عضادةَ سَمْحَجٍ * بسَرَاتِها نَدَبٌ له وكُلومُ
(Or a braying wild ass, busy at the flank of a long-backed she-ass, on whose back are scars and wounds from him.)
So he made عمل act upon العضادة; had it been عامل, it would have been clearer in Arabic. Likewise when you say of a man: ضرّابٌ and ضروبٌ (a great striker), you do not make them act upon anything, because they are [words of] praise; but when the poet needs to make them act, he does so. Someone recited to me:
* وبالفأسِ ضرَّابٌ رءوس الكرانفِ *
(And with the axe, a great striker of the bases of palm-stalks.)
Its singular is كرنافة, which are the bases of the roof [Translator's note: so in the source; الكرانيف are usually the broad bases of palm fronds]. It is said: الحُقْب is eighty years, the year being three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is a thousand years by the reckoning of the people of this world.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْداً وَلاَ شَرَاباً﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying]: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: they taste in it neither the coolness of drink nor drink. Some said: they do not taste in it any coolness (برداً), meaning sleep. Al-Farrāʾ said: sleep does cool the one who has it; the thirsty one sleeps and is cooled by sleep.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿جَزَآءً وِفَاقاً﴾.
In accordance with their deeds.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, read it lightened: "كِذَاباً", while ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī made it heavy (doubled).
It is an eloquent Yemeni dialect: they say كذبت به كِذَّاباً (I denied it utterly), and خرّقت القميص خِرّاقاً (I tore the shirt to pieces); every فعّلت has, in their dialect, a maṣdar on the pattern فِعّال, doubled. One of their Bedouins said to me [123/b] at al-Marwa, asking me for a legal ruling: "Is shaving (الحلق) dearer to you, or shortening (القِصّار)?"
One of Banū Kilāb recited to me:
لقدْ طالَ ما ثَبَّطْتَنِى عنْ صَحابتىِ * وعن حِوَجٍ قِضَّاؤها من شِفائيا
(Long indeed have you held me back from my companions and from needs whose fulfilment is my cure.)
Al-Kisāʾī used to read lightened: ﴿لا يَسْمَعون فِيهَا لغْوا ولا كِذَاباً﴾ (35), because it is not tied to a verb that makes it a maṣdar; and he read doubled: ﴿وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً﴾, because كذّبوا ties الكذّاب to being a maṣdar. What he said is good. Its meaning: they hear no idle talk in it — He means: falsehood — nor كذاب, i.e. they do not call one another liars.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is put in the genitive in its case-ending, and also in the nominative. Likewise: ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَاباً﴾: "الرحمنُ" is put in the nominative and [also] in the genitive in its case-ending; the nominative in it is more common. He said: al-Farrāʾ reads (ربِّ) in the genitive and "الرحمنُ" in the nominative.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: His saying «عمّ»: composed of the genitive preposition «عن» and the interrogative «ما» whose alif has been dropped; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يتساءلون».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The preposition «عن النبأ» is a badal (substitute) of the preposition before it and is attached to what it is attached to.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «الذي»: naʿt (adjective) of «نبأ»; the preposition «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «مختلفون».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (كلا سيعلمون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (ثم كلا سيعلمون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the resumptive one before it.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «الجبال»: a noun conjoined to {الأَرْضَ}; «أوتادا»: a noun conjoined to {مِهَادًا}.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «وخلقناكم» is conjoined to the earlier clause {أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ}; «أزواجا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «لنخرج» is genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The singular of «ألفاف» is لِفّ, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: His saying «يوم»: a badal (substitute) of {يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ}; the preposition «في الصور» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause «فتأتون» is conjoined to «ينفخ»; and «أفواجا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تأتون».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «وفتحت» is conjoined to the clause {يُنْفَخُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The preposition «للطاغين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of {مِرْصَادًا}; «مآبا»: second khabar (predicate) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: His saying «لابثين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الطاغين»; the preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لابثين»; «أحقابا»: an adverb attached to «لابثين».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «لا يذوقون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in {لابِثِينَ}, i.e.: remaining, not tasting.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: (إلا حميما وغساقا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] Connected excepted (mustathnā muttaṣil) from {شَرَابًا}.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «جزاء»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e.: they are recompensed with a recompense; and «وفاقا» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «كِذَّابا»: maṣdar (verbal noun) of كذّبوا; the maṣdar of فَعَّل is التفعيل and الفِعّال.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The wāw is a conjunction; «كلَّ»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أحصينا"; the implied clause is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا}, and the clause «أحصيناه» is explicative; «كتابا»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object), and this maṣdar is synonymous in meaning with its governing word.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «فذوقوا» is resumptive, and the clause «فلن نزيدكم» is conjoined to the resumptive one; «عذابا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «حدائق»: badal (substitute) of {مَفَازًا}, a substitute of the whole for the whole; these very things were made the place of triumph.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «لا يسمعون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «لحدائق».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «جزاء»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the preposition «من ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar «جزاء»; «عطاء»: badal (substitute) of «جزاء»; and «حسابا»: naʿt (adjective) of «عطاء», and it is a maṣdar put in the place of the adjective.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «رب»: badal (substitute) of {رَبِّكَ}; «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to the earth; «الرحمن»: naʿt (adjective) of the second «رب»; and the clause «لا يملكون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الرحمن».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «يوم»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يَمْلِكُونَ}; «صفا»: ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause «لا يتكلمون» is a second ḥāl; «مَنْ»: a relative noun, badal (substitute) of the wāw in «يتكلمون»; and «صوابا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «اليوم» is a badal (substitute); «الحق» is the khabar (predicate) of «ذلك»; and the conditional clause is conjoined to the resumptive one: «ذلك اليوم الحق». The two objects of «اتخذ»: الإيمان (faith), implied, and «مآبا»; the preposition «إلى ربه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مآبا».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «عذابا»: second object; the adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt (adjective) of «عذابا», i.e.: being on the day; «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «نظر» may be transitive by itself; «يا»: a particle of alerting (tanbīh); and the clause «يقول» is conjoined to the clause «ينظر».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (عم): its origin is (عن ما). The alif was dropped because a preposition entered upon (ما), which is interrogative, to distinguish between the interrogative and the declarative; the fatḥa indicates the alif. Ibn Kathīr, in the transmission of al-Bazzī from him, paused on it with hāʾ to make the vowel clear, so that the alif would not be dropped and what indicates it dropped too. The body of the other readers paused with vowellessness. Likewise whatever resembles it of the interrogative (ما) when a preposition enters upon it: this is its rule. Keeping the alif is not permissible except in poetry, just as dropping the alif is not permissible when (ما) is declarative, as in (وما الله بغافل عما يعملون).

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (عن النبإ): a badal (substitute) from (ما) with the preposition repeated. It is also said that the implied form is "They ask one another about the news", then the verb was omitted because the first indicates it; so the first (عن) is attached to the overt (يتساءلون) and the second to the implied one.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying (مهادا): the second object of (جعل), and likewise (أوتادا) and likewise (سباتا), because (جعل) means "made into" (صيّر); likewise (لباسا) and (معاشا).
His saying (وخلقناكم أزواجا): (أزواجا) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We originated you differing: males and females, short and tall". (خلق) means "originated", which is why it passes to only one object.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (سراجا): an object of (جعلنا), which here means "We created"; it too passes to one object, and it does not mean "We made into" as in what preceded.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying (ألفافا): it is the plural of (لف); one says (نبات لف) and (لفيف) when it is dense. It is also said that it is a plural of a plural, as if the singular were (لفاء) and (ألف), like (حمراء) and (أحمر); then (لفاء) is pluralised as (لف), as you say (حمراء) and (حمر); then (لف) is pluralised as (ألفاف), as you say (قفل) and (أقفال).

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying (يوم ينفخ): a badal (substitute) from the first (يوم).
His saying (أفواجا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (تأتون).

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying (لابثين فيها أحقابا): (أحقابا) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān). Whoever reads it (لبثين) likened it to what is an innate quality in man, such as (حذر) "wary" and (فرق) "fearful"; this is far-fetched, because tarrying is not among what is an innate quality in man, and the pattern faʿil is only for what is innate in a thing, and tarrying is not innate. (أحقاب) is an adverbial in both aspects.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying (لا يذوقون): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (لابثين). It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of (أحقاب); it bears the pronoun because it is a verb, so making it overt is not necessary, even though it runs as an adjective of something other than what it belongs to. It is permissible for it to be a naʿt of (أحقاب) only because of the pronoun in (فيها) referring back to (الأحقاب). Had an active participle been in the position of (يذوقون), it would have been necessary to make the pronoun overt if you made it an adjective of (أحقاب).

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (إلا حميما): a badal (substitute) from (برد) if you take (البرد) from coolness. If you make it sleep, then (إلا حميما) is an exception not of the same kind as the first.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying (كذابا): whoever reads it with doubling makes it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of (كذب) [kadhdhaba], with the alif added in it as it was added in (إكراما). As for their saying (تكذيبا), they made the tāʾ a compensation for the doubling of the ʿayn and the yāʾ a substitute for the alif, altering its beginning as they altered its end. The origin of the maṣdar of a quadriliteral verb is to come with the number of letters of the past, with an added alif and a change of vowels. They also said (تكلما), so the maṣdar came with the number of letters of the past without an added alif, and that is because of its many letters; the lām was given ḍamma and not kasra because there is no noun in the language on the pattern tafaʿʿil, and they did not give it fatḥa lest it resemble the past. Al-Kisāʾī read it (كذابا) without doubling, making it the maṣdar of (كاذب كذابا) [Translator's note: printed «مصدرى»]. It is also said that it is the maṣdar of (كذب), as you say (كتبت كتابا).

mekki-muskil:29-29.t:
His saying (وكل شيء أحصيناه كتابا): (كتاب) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because (أحصيناه) means "We wrote it". (كل) is accusative with an implied verb, i.e. "And We enumerated everything — We enumerated it". The nominative is permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying (جزاء وعطاء): two maṣdars, and (حسابا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (عطاء).
His saying (رب السموات): whoever reads it in the nominative and (الرحمن) in the genitive takes it with an implied (هو), and (الرحمن) is a naʿt of (ربك). Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a badal (substitute) from (ربك). Whoever reads it in the nominative and (الرحمن) in the nominative makes it a mubtadaʾ and (الرحمن) its khabar (predicate), or a naʿt of it, with (لا يملكون) the khabar. Whoever reads (الرحمن) in the genitive and (رب) in the nominative makes it a naʿt of (ربك). Whoever reads (الرحمن) in the genitive and (رب) in the genitive makes it a naʿt of (رب), and (رب السموات) is a badal from (ربك). Whoever reads (رب) in the genitive and (الرحمن) in the nominative puts it in the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Most Merciful", or, if you wish, as a mubtadaʾ with (لا يملكون) as the khabar.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t:
His saying (صفا لا يتكلمون): two ḥāls (circumstantials).
His saying (إلا من أذن له الرحمن): (من) is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in (يتكلمون), or in the position of the accusative as an exception.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿عم﴾: «عن» is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the elided alif, in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by ﴿عن﴾; the alif of interrogative «ما» was elided because the preposition entered upon it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتساءلون﴾.
﴿يتساءلون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿عم يتساءلون﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿عن النبأ﴾: «عن» is a preposition, and «النبأ» is a noun in the genitive by ﴿عن﴾, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "they ask one another" (يتساءلون).
﴿العظيم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿النبأ﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿النبأ﴾.
﴿هم﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿فيه﴾: «في» is a preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on kasra, in the position of a genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مختلفون﴾.
﴿مختلفون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾, nominative by the wāw, because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause ﴿هم فيه مختلفون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿سيعلمون﴾: the sīn is a particle of futurity, and «يعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the object of «سيعلمون» is omitted, i.e. "they will come to know what befalls them"; the clause ﴿سيعلمون...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿سيعلمون﴾: the sīn is a particle of futurity, and «يعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the object of «سيعلمون» is omitted, i.e. "they will come to know what befalls them"; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and jussive.
﴿نجعل﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn, the lām being given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (We).
﴿الأرض﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿نجعل﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿مهادا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿نجعل﴾, accusative by the fatḥa; «الجعل» (making) here has the meaning of "causing to become"; or «الجعل» has the meaning of creating, and ﴿مهادا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿والجبال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «الجبال» is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned in the previous ayah.
﴿أوتادا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa. The clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وخلقناكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «خلق» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the mīm is a sign of the plural.
﴿أزواجا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of ﴿خلقناكم﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وجعلنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «جعل» is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿نومكم﴾: «نوم» is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿جعل﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿سباتا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿جعل﴾, accusative by the fatḥa; «الجعل» (making) here has the meaning of "causing to become"; or «الجعل» has the meaning of creating, and ﴿سباتا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وجعلنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «جعل» is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿الليل﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿جعل﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿لباسا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿جعل﴾, accusative by the fatḥa. «الجعل» (making) here has the meaning of "causing to become", or the meaning of creating, ﴿لباسا﴾ [then] being a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وجعلنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «جعل» is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿النهار﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿جعل﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿معاشا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿جعل﴾, accusative by the fatḥa. «الجعل» (making) here has the meaning of "causing to become", or the meaning of creating, ﴿معاشا﴾ [then] being a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وبنينا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «بنى» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿فوقكم﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بنينا﴾; the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿سبعا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿شدادا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سبعا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وجعلنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «جعل» is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿سراجا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿جعلنا﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿وهاجا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سراجا﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; «الجعل» (making) here has the meaning of creating only; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وأنزلنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «أنزل» is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿من المعصرات﴾: «من» is a preposition, and «المعصرات» is a noun in the genitive by the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾.
﴿ماء﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿ثجاجا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ثجاجا﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; it is evidently a naʿt of ﴿ماء﴾], accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿نجعل﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿لنخرج﴾: the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and «نخرج» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن» implied after the lām, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن نخرج﴾ is in the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾.
﴿به﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on kasra, in the position of a genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿نخرج﴾.
﴿حبا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿ونباتا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿نباتا﴾ is a noun conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وجنات﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «جنات» is a noun conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra, because it is a sound feminine plural.
﴿ألفافا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جنات﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿يوم﴾: the noun of «إن», accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; it is muḍāf.
﴿الفصل﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (it).
﴿ميقاتا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿كان﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the clause ﴿إن يوم الفصل...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿يوم﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿يوم الفصل﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿ينفخ﴾: an imperfect verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named).
﴿في﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) preposition.
﴿الصور﴾: a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of a nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿فتأتون﴾: the fāʾ is an indeclinable conjunction, and «تأتون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿تأتون﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿ينفخ﴾.
﴿أفواجا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «تأتون», accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وفتحت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «فتحت» is a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿السماء﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿فكانت﴾: the fāʾ is an indeclinable conjunction, and «كانت» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, the tāʾ being for the feminine; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya" (it), referring back to «السماء».
﴿أبوابا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿فتحت﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ينفخ﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وسيرت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «سيرت» is a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿الجبال﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿فكانت﴾: the fāʾ is an indeclinable conjunction, and «كانت» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, the tāʾ being for the feminine; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya" (it), referring back to «السماء» [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently carried over from the previous ayah; here the pronoun refers back to «الجبال»].
﴿سرابا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿سيرت﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ينفخ﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿جهنم﴾: the noun of «إن», accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿كانت﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, the tāʾ being for the feminine; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya" (it).
﴿مرصادا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿كان﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the clause ﴿إن جهنم...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿للطاغين﴾: the lām is an indeclinable (mabnī) preposition, and «الطاغين» is a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مرصادا﴾.
﴿مآبا﴾: the second khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿لابثين﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الطاغين», accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the source; as a sound masculine plural, «لابثين» is accusative by the yāʾ].
﴿فيها﴾: «في» is a preposition, and ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of a genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لابثين﴾.
﴿أحقابا﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to ﴿لابثين﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يذوقون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿فيها﴾: «في» is a preposition, and ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يذوقون﴾.
﴿بردا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is a particle for reinforcing the negation.
﴿شرابا﴾: a noun conjoined to ﴿بردا﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿لا يذوقون﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿لابثين﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle, and restriction [Translator's note: so in the source («أداة وحصر»); presumably "a particle of exception and restriction" was intended].
﴿حميما﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿شرابا﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿وغساقا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «غساقا» is a noun conjoined to ﴿حميما﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿جزاء﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense", accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿وفاقا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جزاء﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿إنهم﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with no grammatical position; the hāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a nominative, the noun of «إن» [Translator's note: so in the source; the noun of «إن» is in the position of an accusative], and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿كانوا﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hum" (they) [Translator's note: so in the source; the noun of «كانوا» is the overt attached wāw of the plural].
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يرجون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿حسابا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿لا يرجون﴾ is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of kāna; the clause ﴿كانوا لا يرجون﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; and the [whole] clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وكذبوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «كذب» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿بآياتنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوا﴾.
﴿كذابا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in some dialects; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿وكل﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. «كل» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, accusative (manṣūb) by preoccupation (ʿalā al-ishtighāl), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿شيء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿أحصيناه﴾: a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); and the hāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi.
﴿كتابا﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿وكل شيء أحصيناه﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿فذوقوا﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of resumption indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «ذوقوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable on the elision of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿فلن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity, indeclinable on sukūn.
﴿نزيدكم﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu" (We); the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿عذابا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿لن نزيكم﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, for «لن نزيدكم»] is conjoined to ﴿فذوقوا﴾, and the clause ﴿فذوقوا﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿للمتقين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿مفازا﴾: the postponed noun of «إن», accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿حدائق﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿مفازا﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿وأعنابا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أعنابا» is conjoined to ﴿حدائق﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
