﴿وكواعب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «كواعب» is conjoined to ﴿حدائق﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿أترابا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كواعب﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿وكأسا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «كأسا» is conjoined to ﴿حدائق﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿دهاقا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كأسا﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يسمعون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسمعون﴾.
﴿لغوا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is negating.
﴿كذابا﴾: conjoined to ﴿لغوا﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿لا يسمعون﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿جزاء﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense", accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.
﴿ربك﴾: a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جزاء﴾.
﴿عطاء﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿جزاء﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿حسابا﴾: a naʿt of ﴿عطاء﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿رب﴾: a badal (substitute), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿السماوات﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿والأرض﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الأرض» is conjoined to «السماوات», genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «ما» is a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a genitive, conjoined to «السماوات».
﴿بينهما﴾: «بين» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾; the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. The pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الرحمن﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رب﴾, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يملكون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿منه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يملكون﴾.
﴿خطابا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿لا يملكون﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الرحمن﴾.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لا يملكون﴾.
﴿يقوم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الروح﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «يقوم», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿والملائكة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الملائكة» is conjoined to «الروح», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿صفا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يتكلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil; the clause ﴿لا يتكلمون﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, a badal (substitute) from the fāʿil of ﴿يتكلمون﴾.
﴿أذن﴾: a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أذن﴾.
﴿الرحمن﴾: the fāʿil of «أذن», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿أذِنَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿وقال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «قال» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿صوابا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أذن﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿ذلك﴾: «ذا» is a demonstrative indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance, and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿اليوم﴾: a badal (substitute), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الحق﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), indeclinable on fatḥa, and «من» is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ.
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿شاء﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of ﴿مَن﴾.
﴿اتخذ﴾: a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of a jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition indeclinable on fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the source; «إلى» ends in an alif and is indeclinable on sukūn].
﴿ربه﴾: a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on kasra, in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿مآبا﴾.
﴿مآبا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿ذلك اليوم﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with no grammatical position; and ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), the noun of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿أنذرناكم﴾: «أنذر» is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the clause ﴿أنذرناكم﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿عذابا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿قريبا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذابا﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عذابا﴾.
﴿ينظر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿المرء﴾: the fāʿil of «ينظر», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿ينظر المرء﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi.
﴿قدمت﴾: «قدم» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, and the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿يداه﴾: «يدا» is the fāʿil of «قدم», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the alif; the hāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿قدمت يداه﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿ويقول﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿يقول﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الكافر﴾: the fāʿil of «يقول», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿يقول الكافر﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿ينظر المرء﴾.
﴿يا﴾: a particle for drawing attention (tanbīh).
﴿ليتني﴾: «ليت» is an abrogating, accusative-governing particle indeclinable on fatḥa; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of ﴿ليت﴾; the clause ﴿يا ليتني﴾ is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿كنت﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on sukūn, and the tāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a nominative, the noun of kāna.
﴿ترابا﴾: the khabar of «كنت», accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿كنت﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of ﴿ليت﴾.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: That is, it lies in wait for whoever disobeys Allah, glory be to Him, and abandons obedience to Him. Al-Ḥasan said: No one enters Paradise until he passes by the Fire. In Arabic, مرصاد is from رصدت ("I watched / lay in wait"), so I am راصد, and مرصاد is for intensification (taktīr). He said «كانت» and did not say مرصادة because it does not run on the verb, so it became a form of relation (nasab).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
That is, their place of return is to it. آب يؤوب means "to return", as the poet said: [mukhallaʿ al-basīṭ] 524-
وكلّ ذي غيبة يئوب ... وغائب الموت لا يؤوب
(Everyone who is absent returns, but the one absent through death does not return.)

nahhas-irab:23-24.t:
لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً (23) لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً وَلا شَراباً (24) لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً (23): this is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī. ʿAlqama, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it «لبثين» without the alif. Objection has been raised against this reading, and it was said: it is a solecism (laḥn) and not permissible, [as is] هو حذر زيدا ("he is wary of Zayd"), even though Sībawayh permitted it and recited: [al-kāmil] 525-
حذر أمورا لا تضير وآمن ... ما ليس منجيه من الأقدار
(Wary of things that do no harm, and feeling safe from what will not save him from the decrees of fate.)
And al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-kāmil] 526-
أو مسحل عمل عضادة سمحج ... بسراته ندب لها وكلوم
(Or a wild ass busy at the flank of a long-backed she-ass, on whose back are scars and wounds from her.)
Except that Sībawayh recited it as «أو مسحل شنج». Some people said: it is a solecism because one only says حذر, and likewise the pattern فَعِل is for someone in whose nature wariness is ingrained; as for one who stays (اللّابث), that has nothing to do with this.
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the first view, it is a mistake; this does not resemble your saying حذر زيدا, because أحقابا is an adverb (ẓarf), and what is intransitive can pass on to an adverb. As for the second, it is binding, except that it is permissible on a remote [interpretation].
The reading لابثين is clear and good. As for the argument of the one who argued for لبثين from what Shuʿba related from Abū Isḥāq, who said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «لبثين» — there is no proof in it, because Abū Isḥāq did not meet ʿAbd Allāh; had its chain of transmission (isnād) been connected there would be proof in it. These things are taken from the reading of ʿAbd Allāh by means that do not establish proof: a broken chain, or from written copies in which لابثين may be written without the alif, so that its reader imagines it to be «لبثين».
There is a difficulty in this verse because of His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً, while they will never come out of it. Among the best things said about it is that Qatāda said: لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً — [ages] that have no end. On this interpretation it is the plural; the singular حقبة has the plural حقب, and أحقاب is a plural of the plural, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 527-
وكنّا كندماني جذيمة حقبة ... من الدّهر حتّى قيل لن يتصدّعا
(We were like the two boon companions of Jadhīma for an age of time, until it was said: they will never part.)
It is also possible that أحقاب is the plural of حقب; we have already mentioned what the exegetes said about its meaning.
As for the lexicographers, they say that الحقب and الحقبة apply to a short and to a long period of time. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: We asked Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd about the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً, and he said: What is the meaning of this limitation? When we set a limit to something and say, "I will stay with you a day", the force of the speech is that you will not stay after that day. Then he did not answer us about it for some thirty-odd years. [ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said:] I looked into it, and it occurred to me that by it are meant the disobedient monotheists; then I looked and found that after it comes "they used not to expect a reckoning", so I knew that this was not the answer. He said: The answer in my view is that the meaning is "staying in the earth for ages", so the pronoun refers back to the earth because it has been mentioned before, and the pronoun in لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً وَلا شَراباً refers back to the Fire, because it too has been mentioned before.
He said: I did not know of an answer from Abū al-ʿAbbās on it. Abū Jaʿfar said: So I asked Abū Isḥāq about it, and he said: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: The meaning is "staying in it for ages whose description is this", i.e. they will be punished with this punishment in these ages, tasting nothing in them but scalding water (الحميم) and pus (الغسّاق), and after this punishment they will be punished with other kinds of punishment besides this. This is a clear, reasoned answer, and it is the view of Ibn Kaysān: «لا يذوقون» is then a naʿt (adjective) of الأحقاب.
The scholars differed about His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً. It was said: that is, they will not taste in it any coolness that would cool the blaze from them. It was also said: [it means] sleep, as the poet said: [al-kāmil] 528-
بردت مراشفها عليّ فصدّني ... عنها وعن قبلاتها البرد
(Her lips grew cool to me, and sleep turned me away from her and from her kisses.)
— that is, sleep and drowsiness. البرد may also be calm and stillness, as the poet said: [al-rajaz] 529- اليوم يوم بارد سمومه (Today is a day whose hot wind is still.) And البرد may be what has no hardship in it, as it is related: «الصوم في الشتاء الغنيمة الباردة» ("Fasting in winter is the cool booty"), which is booty in which there is no heat of weapons. And one says: بردت حرّه ("I cooled his burning"), as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 530-
وعطّل قلوصي في الرّكاب فإنّها ... ستبرد أكبادا وتبكي بواكيا
(Leave my young she-camel without a rider among the mounts, for she will cool [burning] livers and make weepers weep.)
The soundest of these views is the first, because البرد is not one of the names of sleep; one only contrives it, saying of sleep that it is برد because it calms thirst. What is obligatory is that the interpretation of the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, be taken according to the apparent and well-known meanings, unless there is evidence for something else.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Abū Razīn and Ibrāhīm said: الغسّاق is the pus that flows. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda said: الغساق is what stinks. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الغساق is bitter cold (الزمهرير). Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are not contradictory, because what flows from their skins may be stinking and intensely cold. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: غساق with the doubled consonant (tashdīd) is preferable, because one says غسقت عينه, i.e. "his eye watered", so غسّاق is like سيّال, an intensive of غاسق. Someone else said: from this the night is called غاسق, because of its covering and its onrush, as a flood rushes in. It was also said: الحميم is excepted from الشراب, and الغسّاق is excepted from البرد.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: جَزاءً is a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose verb is indicated by what precedes it. وِفاقاً is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
It was said: يرجون means "they fear", because whoever hopes for something is overtaken by fear of missing it, so one of the two fears is given prominence, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 531-
إذا لسعته النّحل لم يرج لسعها ... وخالفها في بيت نوب عوامل
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he goes after them into a hive of busy bees.)
It was also said: الرجاء here has its usual meaning, i.e. they do not hope for the reward of the reckoning.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
It is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It has been related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كِذَّاباً with the first and the second without doubling (takhfīf); this is an irregular (shādhdh) transmission. But it is soundly established from al-Kisāʾī that he read the second without doubling, as the poet said: [majzūʾ al-kāmil] 532-
فصدقتهم وكذّبتهم ... والمرء ينفعه كذابه
(I told them the truth and I lied to them, and a man may profit from his lying.)
كذّاب with the doubling is, according to some of the Kufans, a Yemeni dialect form, and this yields little benefit. Rather, the view of Sībawayh ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears here in the source.] is that it is in reality the maṣdar of كذّب, even if the usage is يكذّب تكذيبا ("to belie greatly"). There is a subtle point of grammar in it: bringing this tāʾ into تكذيب when it has no basis in the verb. And it may be asked: what is the evidence that the original is كذّاب? We will explain it according to the school of Sībawayh, Allah willing. The way of the verb, when it is of four letters, is that an alif is added to its past form in the maṣdar, so you say أكرم إكراما and انطلق انطلاقا; this is a consistent analogy (qiyās), and likewise كذّب كذّابا and تكلم كلاما. Then they said كذب تكذيبا, and Sībawayh said: they replaced the added (doubled) ʿayn with tāʾ and changed the alif to yāʾ, so they altered its beginning as they altered its end. Abū Jaʿfar said: As for تكلّم تكلما, they brought the past form and did not add an alif because of its many letters, and they put a ḍamma on the lām; Sībawayh said: because there is no تَفْعَل among nouns.

nahhas-irab:29-30.t:
وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْناهُ: كلّ is accusative by an implied verb, so that what the verb governs is conjoined to what the verb governs, as the poet said: [mukhallaʿ al-basīṭ] 533-
أصبحت لا أحمل السّلاح ولا ... أملك رأس البعير إن نفرا
والذّئب أخشاه إن مررت به ... وحدي وأخشى الرّياح والمطرا
(I have come to the point where I cannot carry weapons, nor control the camel's head if it bolts; and the wolf I fear if I pass by it alone, and I fear the winds and the rain.)
The nominative is also permissible, as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the Kufans say: [it is nominative] by the pronoun referring back to it. كِتاباً is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Some grammarians say: what governs it is implied, i.e. كتبناه كتابا, meaning "We recorded its number, its sum and its measure, so that nothing of it is hidden from Us" — كتابا. It was also said: what governs it is «أحصيناه», because أحصيناه and كتبناه are one [in meaning]. Al-Ḥasan said: I asked Abū Burda about the verse in the Quran that is hardest on the people of the Fire, and he said: The Messenger of Allah recited فَذُوقُوا فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذاباً (30) and said: "The people have been destroyed by their disobedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He." And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: Nothing harder was revealed concerning the people of the Fire than His saying: فَذُوقُوا فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذاباً (30).

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: حَدائِقَ is a badal (substitute) for «مفاز». المفاز is attaining what a person loves. Ibn ʿAbbās said: الحدائق are densely intertwined trees. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: [it is the garden] that has walls around it. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is likewise in the language; one says قد حدق بالقوم ("it surrounded the people"), as the poet said: [al-khafīf] 534- وقد حدقت بي المنيّة (And death has surrounded me.)

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: It is conjoined (maʿṭūf). The singular is كاعب, and كواعب is for the plural and the feminine.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: That is, filled. It is derived from دهقه, [said] when one presses hard upon him in succession.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: Al-Kisāʾī read «كذابا», and it departs from the reading of the majority. It may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) of كاذب كذابا, and it may be a maṣdar of كذب, as you say صام صياما; this is more likely. That is: they will not hear in it falsehood that is uttered idly, nor lying.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
جَزاءً is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and likewise عَطاءً. حِساباً is its naʿt (adjective), i.e. a sufficient gift, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 535-
ونغني وليد الحيّ إن كان جائعا ... ونحسبه إن كان ليس بجائع
(We enrich the child of the tribe if he is hungry, and give him his fill even if he is not hungry.)
Mujāhid said: حسابا [means] according to their deeds.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
[Nominative in both] is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĀṣim read both in the genitive. Ibn Muḥayṣin, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ḥamza read the first in the genitive and the second in the nominative; this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because the first is near and the second distant. A group of grammarians disagreed with him, saying there is nothing in its distance that requires the nominative, because nothing separates the two that would require this. Whoever puts both in the nominative makes the first nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the second a naʿt (adjective) of it, the khabar (predicate) being لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطاباً; it is also possible that the first is nominative by an implied هو. Whoever puts both in the genitive makes them a naʿt or a badal (substitute) of the genitive noun. Whoever puts the first in the genitive and the second in the nominative makes the second a mubtadaʾ, or implies a mubtadaʾ.
يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ وَقالَ صَواباً (38) يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الروح is an angel of immense form. Someone else related from him that he said: الروح are the spirits of people, standing with the angels in the interval between the two blasts, before they are returned to the bodies. Al-Shaʿbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الروح is Jibrāʾīl, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: الروح are the children of Adam. Ibn Zayd said: الروح is the Quran. Mujāhid said: الروح are [beings] in the forms of the children of Adam but are not of them. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no evidence whose knowledge would indicate which of these views is soundest decisively, whether by instruction from the Messenger or by clear indication; and it is something ignorance of which does no harm. If someone were to say: these things the scholars mentioned are not contradictory, and it is possible that all of them are meant, he would not be reproached. [Translator's note: the Arabic of the last two sentences is somewhat garbled in the source («لا دليل فعلمه يدلّ…», «ويجوز أن يكون هذا كلها لها لما عنّف»); the sense has been rendered as best it can be read.] وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا: [صفّا] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ is in the position of the accusative.
إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ: «من» may be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for the wāw, or in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā), i.e. except one whom the Most Merciful permits to speak. وَقالَ صَواباً: [i.e.] of the truth. ʿIkrima interpreted the meaning otherwise. Abū Jaʿfar said: [his interpretation is] "and said what is right in this world", i.e. said: there is no god but Allah.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَقُّ: [الحقّ] is a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, i.e. possessing truth. فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ مَآباً: i.e. a means of salvation [leading to] a place of return, that is, righteous deeds in this world. [Translator's note: the source reads «نجاء مآب», apparently a corruption, perhaps of «نجاة» or «سبيل».]

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
[إِنـ]ـَّا أَنْذَرْناكُمْ عَذاباً قَرِيباً [Translator's note: the opening letters of the Quranic phrases in this entry are cut off in the source.]
[قريبا] is a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, or of an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. a near time. [يـ]ـوْمَ يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ
The clause is in the position of the genitive, i.e. the day of his looking. يَقُولُ الْكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُراباً
[تُراباً] is the khabar (predicate) of كنت. Some grammarians permitted ليتني قائما ("would that I [were] standing"), saying: because «كان» is frequent after ليت, so it was omitted. [Translator's note: «تنثر» in the source is read as «تكثر» ("is frequent").]

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The original is «عن ما»; the alif was dropped to distinguish between the interrogative and the declarative [ما], because the meaning is: "about what thing are they asking one another?" Al-Farrāʾ reported that the meaning is "for what thing are they asking one another?" Abū Jaʿfar said: «عن» in the sense of the lām is not known. The construction is: "they ask one another about the great news", and it was omitted because the speech indicates it.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: [الَّذِي is] in the position of khafḍ (genitive).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
كَلَّا: it has been said that it is the full stop, i.e. the matter is not as the polytheists claimed in denying the resurrection.
«ستعلمون» ] is a threat to them; in the reading of al-Ḥasan [with tāʾ] the construction is: "say to them: you will know". «ثم كلا ستعلمون»: يعلمون is conjoined to it; and the reading of the generality is with yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: [مِهاداً] may be a singular, and it may be the plural of مهده «[Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for «مَهْد».]».

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: [أَوْتاداً is] conjoined to it; it is the plural of وتد. Whoever assimilates says ودّ. Assimilation is not permissible in the plural, because the alif has separated the two letters.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَخَلَقْناكُمْ أَزْواجاً (8): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. of kinds — i.e. male and female, short and tall; so He, Mighty and Majestic, drew their attention to His power.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t: وَجَعَلْنا نَوْمَكُمْ سُباتاً (9): two objects; and likewise وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً (10), i.e. it covers you and envelops you like garments, i.e. We did this so that you may sleep in it and rest, as Qatāda said: لباسا means a rest.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: I.e. possessing livelihood; i.e. We made it bright so that they may live in it and go about their business, as Mujāhid said: معاشا — in which you go about and seek of the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: The hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa, in سَبْعاً] was dropped because the eloquent usage is to treat السماء as feminine. شِداداً is the plural of شديدة; it is not pluralised as فعلاء [i.e. أشدّاء] because of the heaviness of the doubling.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: وَجَعَلْنا سِراجاً: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَهَّاجاً, i.e. shining.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned two views of the exegetes: that المعصرات are the winds, and the clouds. The more appropriate of the two is that they are the clouds, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic, مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ, and He did not say بالمعصرات; and as was read before Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth; he said:
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me, from his father; he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to me, from al-Minhāl, from Qays ibn al-Sakan, from Ibn Masʿūd; he said: Allah, glory be to Him, sends the winds, and they take up the water and make it run in the clouds, and they yield [it] as the milch camel yields milk. And it is related from Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ماءً ثَجَّاجاً — he said: He says: pouring down. Ibn Yazīd «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps Ibn Zayd.]» said: ثجّاجا means abundant. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is the one known in the speech of the Arabs: one says ثجّ الماء ثجوجا, when it pours down, and ثجّه فلان ثجا, when he pours it in a continuous flow. And in the ḥadīth: "The best pilgrimage is العجّ and الثجّ": العجّ is raising the voice in the talbiya, and الثجّ is pouring out the blood of the sacrificial animals.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَباتاً (15): الحبّ is everything that has a husk, and النبات is grass, herbage and the like.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَجَنَّاتٍ, i.e. the fruit of gardens. أَلْفافاً: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the view of whoever said it is the plural of لفّ, and the view of whoever said it is a plural of a plural — he meant that one says لفّاء and ألفّ, like حمراء and أحمر, then you say ألف «[Translator's note: i.e. لُفّ.]», as one says حمر, and then لفّ is pluralised as ألفاف, as you say خفّ / أخفاف. The first view is closer to correctness, because the exegetes said: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفافاً (16), i.e. all together [i.e. dense], and we know of no disagreement among them about that; so this is the plural of لفّ. And one says لفيف with the same meaning; and نخلة لفّاء means a thick palm. For this reason we said the first is closer to correctness.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: [مِيقاتاً is] the khabar (predicate) of كانَ; if it were outside the Quran, the nominative would be permissible, with كان cancelled.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ is a badal (substitute). فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْواجاً: [أَفْواجاً is] as a ḥāl (circumstantial); one says فوج and فوجة.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t: وَفُتِحَتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ أَبْواباً (19): there are two views on its meaning. It has been said: its meaning is "it was split open and became pathways"; and it has been said: "it was cut up and became pieces like doors", then the kāf was dropped, as you say رأيت فلانا أسدا, i.e. like a lion. And likewise وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ فَكانَتْ سَراباً (20).

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(عمّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتساءلون); (عن النبأ) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being يتساءلون; (الذي) relative noun, in the position of a genitive as a second naʿt (adjective) of النبأ; (فيه) attached to (مختلفون).
The clause «يتساءلون ...» has no grammatical position: an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «(يتساءلون) عن النبأ ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هم فيه مختلفون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).

* Benefits:
- Interrogative (ما):
Its meaning is (أيّ شيء) "what thing", as in the saying of the Exalted (ما هِيَ), (ما لَوْنُها), (وَما تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يا مُوسى). The alif of interrogative (ما) must be dropped when it is governed by a preposition, keeping the fatḥa as an indication of it, as in: فيم, إلام, علام, بم. Al-Kumayt ibn Zayd said:
فتلك ولاة السوء قد طال مكثهم ... فحتام حتام العناء المطوّل
(Those are the evil governors whose stay has grown long ... so until when, until when, this prolonged toil?)
The evidence in it is حتى entering upon interrogative ما, so its alif was dropped. Likewise the saying of the Exalted in the verse we are dealing with (عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ).
As for the saying of Ḥassān:
على ما قام يشتمني ليئم ... كخنزير تمرغ في رماد
(For what reason did a base man rise to revile me ... like a pig that has rolled in ashes?)
this is a poetic licence (ḍarūra shiʿriyya) on which no analogy is drawn.
When interrogative (ما) is compounded with (ذا), its alif is not dropped, as in (لماذا جئت) "why did you come?", because its alif has become medial.

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke, in both places, against the questioning; (السين) for the future; (ثمّ) for conjunction. The clause «سيعلمون (the first)» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سيعلمون (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause, to increase the threat and menace.

safi-cedvel:6-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of affirmation (al-taqrīr); (مهادا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الجبال أوتادا) is like الأرض مهادا and conjoined to it.
The clause «نجعل الأرض ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
8-11 (الواو) conjunction; (أزواجا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the object pronoun in (خلقناكم); (سباتا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and likewise (لباسا, معاشا).
The clause «خلقناكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجعل.
The clause «جعلنا (the first)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجعل.
The clause «جعلنا (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجعل.
The clause «جعلنا (the third)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجعل.
12- (فوقكم) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بنينا), by making it carry the meaning of رفعنا "We raised"; (سبعا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative — and it is an adjective standing for an omitted noun it qualifies, i.e. سموات سبعا "seven heavens" —. The clause «بنينا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجعل ...
13- (سراجا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its governor being جعلنا, by making it carry the meaning of خلقنا "We created" [Note: (سراجا) may be a second object.. and the first object is omitted, i.e. "We made the sun a lamp".].
The clause «جعلنا (the fourth)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجعل ...
14-16 (من المعصرات) attached to (أنزلنا); (اللام) of reason (al-taʿlīl); (نخرج) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نخرج..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (أنزلنا). The clause «أنزلنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجعل..
The clause «نخرج ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(11) معاشا: a mīmī maṣdar meaning livelihood, and what is intended by it is an adverb of time; since its use in the language as a noun of time is not established, an omitted muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "the time of livelihood", as in our saying آتيك طلوع الفجر "I will come to you at the rising of dawn", i.e. at the time of the rising of dawn. Its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn, and it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); the original is معيش — with fatḥa on the yāʾ —: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(13) وهّاجا: a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), resembling the active participle, from the triliteral وهج يوهج, of the pattern-class فتح, or وهج يهج, of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and doubling of the ʿayn, and intensiveness may be intended by it.
(14) المعصرات: plural of المعصرة, feminine of المعصر, a noun for the cloud whose time of raining has come; its pattern is مفعلات, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(ثجّاجا): the intensive of the active participle of the triliteral ثجّ — transitive or intransitive —, of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa.
(15) حبّا: a collective noun whose singular is حبّة; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(16) ألفافا: plural of لفيف, on the pattern فعيل, like شريف and أشراف; or meaning "intertwined", having no singular; or the plural of لفّ with kasra on the lām, like سرّ and أسرار; and the pattern of ألفاف is أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
Simile (al-tashbīh): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهاداً وَالْجِبالَ أَوْتاداً».
He likened the mountains to the pegs of tents that keep them from shaking, just as the mountains keep the earth from swaying with its people.
The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً».
The point of resemblance is covering, because both clothing and the night cover the one wrapped in them. The meaning is: We made it a covering for you from eyes, when you wish to flee from an enemy, or to attack him by night, or to hide many matters that you do not like to be seen.

safi-cedvel:17-20.t:
* I'rab:
The second (يوم) is a badal (substitute) of (ميقاتا) [Note: Or a badal of the noun of إنّ.. or attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأتون).]; (في الصور) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أفواجا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil (agent)..
The clause «إنّ يوم الفصل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان ميقاتا ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «ينفخ في الصور ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تأتون ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause ينفخ [Note: If the adverb (يوم) is attached to (تأتون), the clause is conjoined to the resumptive clause.].
19-20 (الواو) conjunction in both places, and likewise (الفاء) in both places..
The clause «فتحت السماء ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause تأتون [Note: Or conjoined to the clause ينفخ.].
The clause «كانت أبوابا» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause فتحت.
The clause «سيّرت الجبال» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause تأتون [Note: Or conjoined to the clause ينفخ.].
The clause «كانت سرابا ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause سيّرت.

* Morphology:
(19) أبوابا: plural of باب, a non-derived noun (ism jāmid); the alif is converted from a wāw, as is seen in the plural; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas: the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.

* Rhetoric:
The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ فَكانَتْ سَراباً».
For He likened the mountains to a mirage, omitting the particle of comparison and the point of resemblance; what unites them is that both the mountains and the mirage are seen in the form of a thing while not being that thing.

safi-cedvel:21-30.t:
* I'rab:
(للطاغين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مرصادا); (مآبا) a second khabar (predicate) of كانت; (لابثين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of الطاغين; (فيها) attached to (لابثين); (أحقابا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (لابثين); (لا) negative, and the second is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation; (فيها) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of يذوقون [Note: Or attached to (يذوقون).]; (شرابا) conjoined by the wāw to (بردا), accusative; (إلّا) for exception; (حميما) badal (substitute) of (شرابا) [Note: Some made it accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).]; (جزاء) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb [Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative.]; (وفاقا) naʿt (adjective) of (جزاء), accusative..
The clause «إنّ جهنّم كانت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كانت مرصادا ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لا يذوقون ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl of the pronoun of لابثين.
25-29 (لا) negative; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (بآياتنا) attached to (كذّبوا); (كذّابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative; (كلّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation), i.e. "We have enumerated every ..."; (كتابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar [Note: Either because writing is enumeration, or because أحصيناه means "We wrote it" ... It may be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, meaning مكتوبا "written".].
The clause «إنّهم كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لا يرجون ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of كانوا.
The clause «كذّبوا ...» is in the position of a nominative: conjoined to the clause كانوا [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied.].
The clause «(أحصينا) كلّ شيء ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أحصيناه ...» has no grammatical position: explicative (tafsīriyya).
30- (الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition; (الفاء) of reason (taʿlīliyya); (إلّا) for restriction (al-ḥaṣr) ...
(عذابا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «ذوقوا ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm): the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if you denied in the world, then taste the punishment in the Hereafter".. and the implied conditional clause is the object of speech of an implied verb of saying ...
The clause «لن نزيدكم ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason.

* Morphology:
(21) مرصادا: a noun meaning the road, coming on the pattern of the intensive form from the triliteral رصد, meaning "he watched", i.e. it lies in wait for the disbelievers, watching for them; or it is prepared for them and made ready for their punishment.
(23) لابثين: plural of لابث, active participle of the triliteral لبث; its pattern is فاعل. (أحقابا): plural of حقب, with ḍamma then sukūn.. see verse (60) of Surat al-Kahf.
(24) بردا: it may be a noun meaning sleep; sleep is called برد because it cools the one who has it, and this is the dialect of Hudhayl.. And see verse (69) of Surat al-Anbiyāʾ.
(26) وفاقا: an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the four-letter verb وافق; its pattern is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ, and it is used in the place of an adjective for intensiveness.
(28) كذّابا: an aurally transmitted maṣdar of the four-letter verb كذّب; its pattern is فعّال, with kasra on the fāʾ and doubling of the ʿayn, which has fatḥa.
(29) كتابا: a maṣdar meaning writing or meaning enumeration; its pattern is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:31-37.t:
* I'rab:
(للمتّقين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (حدائق) badal (substitute) of (مفازا), accusative like it, and it is denied tanwīn because it is on the pattern of the furthest plurals (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ), and likewise the conjoined (كواعب); (أترابا) naʿt (adjective) of كواعب, accusative ...
The clause «إنّ للمتّقين مفازا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
35-37 (لا) negative, and the second is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation; (فيها) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يسمعون [Note: Or attached to (يسمعون).]; (جزاء) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (26) of the surah.. It may be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. مجازين "recompensed".]; (عطاء) badal of جزاء, accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.. or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يسمعون.]; (حسابا) naʿt of عطاء [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb.] ... (ربّ) badal of ربّك, genitive; (ما) relative noun, in the position of a genitive, conjoined by the wāw to السموات; (الرحمن) naʿt of the second ربّ; (لا) negative; (منه) attached to (يملكون), by making it carry the meaning of ينالون "they obtain".
The clause «لا يسمعون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as naʿt of حدائق.].
The clause «لا يملكون ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl of الرحمن.

* Morphology:
(31) مفازا: a mīmī maṣdar from the triliteral فاز; its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn, so it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is مفوز: the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif ... It may be a noun of place.
(33) كواعب: plural of كاعب, active participle of the triliteral كعبت الجارية, of the pattern-class نصر, "the girl's breasts appeared in swelling"; its pattern is فاعل, and the plural is فواعل.
(34) دهاقا: a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from دهق الكأس "he filled the cup", of the pattern-class فتح — or "he emptied it" — it is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād); and الكأس الدهاق is the full cup; its pattern is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {عَمَّ}: It has preceded that al-Bazzī inserts the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt) in compensation for the alif of interrogative «ما» when pausing. It is transmitted from Ibn Kathīr that he read «عَمَّه» with the hāʾ in continuous recitation (waṣl), treating continuation as pausing. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], Ubayy and ʿIkrima read «عَمَّا» with the alif retained. It has preceded that this is permissible in poetic necessity or in a small amount of speech. From it is:
4464 - على ما قامَ يَشْتِمُني لَئيمٌ ... كخِنْزيرٍ تَمَرَّغَ في رَمادِ
(Over what does a base man stand reviling me, like a pig wallowing in ashes?)
/ And it has preceded that al-Zamakhsharī counted among it {بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي} in Yā Sīn [verse 27]. Concerning «عَمَّ» there are two views. The first, which is the apparent one, is that it is attached to «يتساءلون», this overt verb. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: "The speech is complete at His saying «عَمَّ يتساءلون»; then what the discourse required was that a respondent should answer and say: 'They ask one another about the great news.' So the concision and eloquence of the Qur'an required that the one presenting the argument hasten to give the answer which the situation and the dialogue demand, cutting the argument short and hastening to the point at which they are silenced." The second is that it is attached to an implied (muqaddar) verb, and {عَنِ النبإ العظيم} is attached to this overt verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is reported from Ibn Kathīr that he read «عَمَّهْ» with the hāʾ of pause. This must be one of two things: either continuation is treated as pausing, or he pauses and then begins {يَتَسَآءَلُونَ عَنِ النبإ العظيم}, on the basis that «يتساءلون» is implied (muḍmar), because what comes after it explains it, like something that is left vague and then explained."

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {عَنِ النبإ}: In it is permissible what was permissible in His saying {لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ} [al-Mursalāt: 13], namely being a badal (substitute) and being attached to an implied verb. Here it has in addition the possibility of being attached to the overt verb, while what precedes it is attached to an implied (muḍmar) one, as preceded from al-Zamakhsharī. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Most of the grammarians said: His saying {عَنِ النبإ العظيم} is attached to the overt «يتساءلون», as though He said: 'Why do they ask one another about the news?'" And His saying «عَمَّ» is an interrogative of magnification and exaltation.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {الذي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ}: «مُخْتلفون» is the khabar (predicate) of «هم», and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to it. The relative noun admits all three vowels: [genitive] by following (itbāʿ), and by severance (qaṭʿ) as nominative and accusative.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ، ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ}: The repetition is for emphasis. Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik claimed that it belongs to the category of verbal emphasis (al-tawkīd al-lafẓī), and that the intervention of the conjunction does no harm. The grammarians reject this and call it nothing but conjunction (ʿaṭf), even though it conveys emphasis. The majority read the two verbs in the third person. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Dīnār and Ibn ʿĀmir—with disagreement in the transmission from him—read both with the tāʾ of address. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read the first like al-Ḥasan and the second like the majority. The third person and the second person are both clear.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {مِهَاداً}: a second object, because jaʿl here means "making into" (taṣyīr). It may also mean "creating", in which case «مِهادا» is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial, ḥāl muqaddara), and «أوتاداً» likewise; and it must then also be interpreted as a derived word, i.e. "made firm" (مُثَبَّتات). As for «سُباتاً», the apparent view is that it is a second object. And «لباساً» contains a fine metaphor, and on it is the poet's saying:
4465 - وكم لِظَلامِ الليلِ عندك مِنْ يدٍ ... تُخَبِّرُ أنَّ المانَوِيَّةَ تَكْذِبُ
(How many a favour has the darkness of night done you, proving that the Manichaeans lie.)
The majority read «مِهاداً», while Mujāhid, ʿĪsā and some of the Kufans read «مَهْداً». These two readings have preceded in Sūrat Ṭā Hā, and that the Kufans read «مَهْداً» in Ṭā Hā and al-Zukhruf only; the difference between them was also given there.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {وَهَّاجاً}: al-wahhāj is the shining, glittering thing, from their saying "the jewel wahaja", i.e. glittered. One says wahija yawhaju, like wajila yawjalu, and wahaja yahiju, like waʿada yaʿidu.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {مِنَ المعصرات}: «مِنْ» may be in its basic sense of the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), or it may be causal. This is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, ʿIkrima and Qatāda «بالمُعْصِرات», with the bāʾ instead of «مِنْ». This depends on a disagreement about «المُعْصِرات»: what is meant by it? It was said: the clouds. One says aʿṣarat al-saḥāʾib, i.e. they came close to being squeezed by the winds so that they rain, as you say "ajazza al-zarʿ" when the crop is due to be reaped. From this is "aʿṣarat al-jāriya" when the girl is due to menstruate. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. Ibn Qutayba recited, from Abū al-Najm:
4466 - تَمْشي الهُوَيْنَى ساقِطاً خِمارُها ... قد أَعْصَرَتْ أو قَدْ دَنَا إعْصارُها
(She walks gently, her headscarf slipping; she has reached maturity, or her maturity is near.)
I say: Were it not for interpreting «أَعْصَرَتْ» in this way, «المُعْصَرات» should have been with a fatḥa on the ṣād, as a passive participle, because the winds squeeze them.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ʿIkrima read «بالمُعْصِرات». There are two aspects to it: that the winds which are due to squeeze the clouds are meant, or that the clouds are meant; because if the sending down is from them, then it is by means of them, / just as you say: he gave a dirham from his hand, and he gave it with his hand. From Mujāhid: al-muʿṣirāt are the winds that have whirlwinds (aʿāṣīr). From al-Ḥasan and Qatāda: they are the heavens. Its interpretation is that the water comes down from the sky to the clouds, so it is as though the heavens squeeze, i.e. drive to squeezing and make it possible. If you say: then what is the justification of the one who read «من المُعْصِرات» and explained it as the winds that have whirlwinds, when rain does not come down from the winds? I say: the winds are what produce the clouds and make their udders flow, so it is valid that they be made the starting point of the sending down. It has also come [in a report] that Allah sends the winds, and they carry the water from the sky; if that is sound, then the sending down from them is clear. If you say: Ibn Kaysān mentioned that he took al-muʿṣirāt to mean 'those that bring relief (rain)', yet the one who brings relief is al-ʿāṣir, not al-muʿṣir; one says ʿaṣarahu fa-ʿtaṣara. I say: its justification is that what is meant is 'those which aʿṣarna', i.e. which are due to bring relief (rain)." I say: he means that ʿaṣara in the sense of bringing relief is a triliteral verb, so how could it be said here «مُعْصِرات» with this meaning when it is from the quadriliteral (form IV)? He answered with what has preceded, meaning that the hamza [of form IV] has the sense of entering into the thing.
His saying: {ثَجَّاجاً}: al-thajj is pouring out in great quantity and with force. In the ḥadīth: "The most beloved of deeds to Allah are al-ʿajj and al-thajj": al-ʿajj is raising the voice with the talbiya, and al-thajj is shedding the blood of the sacrificial animals. One says: thajja al-māʾ by itself, i.e. it poured out; and I thajajtuhu, i.e. I poured it out, thajjan and thujūjan. So it is both intransitive and transitive. The poet said:
4467 - إذا رَجَفَتْ فيها رَحَىً مُرْجَحِنَّةٌ ... تَبَعَّجَّ ثَجَّاجاً غَزيرَ الحوافِلِ
(When a heavy, swaying millstone [of a cloud] rumbles in it, it bursts open pouring, with abundant full udders.)
Al-Aʿraj read «ثجَّاحاً» with an undotted ḥāʾ at the end. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The mathājiḥ of water are its pouring places, and water yanthajiḥu in the valley."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {أَلْفَافاً}: There are several views concerning it. The first: that it has no singular. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ألفافاً»: intertwined; it has no singular, like al-awzāʿ and al-akhyāf." The second: that it is the plural of «لِفّ» with kasra on the lām, so it is like sirr and asrār. Abū ʿAlī al-Ṭūsī recited:
4468 - جَنَّةٌ لِفٌّ وعَيْشٌ مُغْدِقُ ... ونَدامى كلُّهم بِيْضٌ زُهُرْ
(A garden dense with trees, an abundant life, and drinking companions all fair and radiant.)
This is the view of most of the lexicographers. The third: that it is the plural of lafīf; al-Kisāʾī said this. Similar to it are sharīf and ashrāf, and shahīd and ashhād. The poet said:
4469 - أحابِيْشُ أَلفْافٌ تبايَنَ فَرْعُهُمْ ... وجِذْمُهُمُ عن نسبةِ المتعرّفِ
(Mixed bands of confederates, their branches and their root at odds with the lineage of the one seeking to know them.)
The fourth: that it is a plural of a plural. That is, the origin is «ألَفُّ» in the masculine and «لَفَّاءُ» in the feminine, like aḥmar and ḥamrāʾ; then both were pluralised as luff, like ḥumr; then luff was pluralised as alfāf, since luff had become of the pattern of qufl and so was pluralised as it is pluralised. Ibn Qutayba said this. However, al-Zamakhsharī said: "I do not think he will find a parallel for it of the type khuḍr and akhḍār, ḥumr and aḥmār." I say: it is as though he considers this view unlikely in that its parallels are not pluralised on the pattern afʿāl, since one does not say khuḍr and akhḍār, nor ḥumr and aḥmār, even though these are plurals of akhḍar/khaḍrāʾ and aḥmar/ḥamrāʾ. But this does not follow, because the plural of a plural is not formed by analogy (lā yanqāsu), and it suffices that it have a parallel among singulars, as you have seen in that luff came to resemble qufl. For this reason they refrained from making broken plurals of mafāʿil and mafāʿīl, for lack of a parallel among singulars on which they could be modelled. The fifth: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If it were said that it is the plural of multaffa, assuming the deletion of the augments, it would be a sound view." I say: this involves a strain for which there is no need. Moreover, most of the grammarians' expressions about "deletion of augments" concern only the diminutive: you say "the diminutive of tarkhīm is by deleting the augments"; and with verbal nouns they say: "this maṣdar (verbal noun) is on the basis of deleting the augments."

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ}: It may be a badal (substitute) for «يومَ الفَصْل» or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) for it, or accusative by an implied «أعني» ("I mean"). «أفْواجاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تأْتون». «فُرَاتاً» has preceded [al-Furqān: 53]. And «فُتِحَتْ» with and without doubling [of the tāʾ] has preceded in al-Zumar.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {لِّلطَّاغِينَ}: It may be a naʿt (adjective) of «مِرْصاداً», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مآباً»—it was its adjective, and when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl. On both these views it is attached to something omitted. It may also be attached to «مِرْصاداً» itself, or to «مآباً» itself, since it means "place of return". Ibn Yaʿmar and Abū ʿAmr al-Minqarī read «أنَّ جهنمَ» with fatḥa on «أنَّ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As giving the reason for the coming of the Hour: that Hell has been a place of ambush for the transgressors, as though it were said: that was to establish the recompense." I say: he means that it is a reason for His saying «يومَ يُنْفَخُ» to the end.
Abū ʿIyāḍ read «في الصُّوَر» with fatḥa on the wāw. Its like has preceded.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {لاَّبِثِينَ}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «للطَّاغِين», and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). Ḥamza read «لَبِثِيْنَ» without an alif, and the rest read «لابِثين» with it. Makkī considered Ḥamza's reading weak; he said: "Whoever reads «لبِثين» likens it to what is an innate trait in a person, such as ḥadhir and fariq; but this is far-fetched, because tarrying (al-lubth) is not something that is innate in a person, and the pattern faʿil is only for what is innate in a person, and tarrying is not innate." Al-Zamakhsharī preferred Ḥamza's reading, saying: "It has been read lābithīn and labithīn, and labith is stronger, because lābith is said of one from whom tarrying has occurred, whereas labith is said only of one whose habit is tarrying, like one who stays crouched in a place and hardly ever leaves it." I say: what al-Zamakhsharī said is more correct. As for Makkī's statement that tarrying is not innate, that is granted; but it has been made hyperbolic and thus treated like innate things.
His saying: {أَحْقَاباً}: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is «لابثين»; this is the well-known view. It was also said that it is governed by His saying «لا يَذُوقون»; this is according to those who allow what is governed by the verb after «لا» to precede it, which is one of the views, and this has preceded in full at the end of al-Fātiḥa. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be accusative as a ḥāl; he said: "There is another aspect: that it be from ḥaqiba ʿāmunā, when its rain and its good are scant, and ḥaqiba so-and-so, when provision misses him, so he is ḥaqib, whose plural is aḥqāb. It is then accusative as a ḥāl from them, meaning: tarrying in it, ḥaqibīn jaḥidīn (deprived and destitute)." The discussion of «الحُقُب» and what has been said about it has preceded in Sūrat al-Kahf.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {لاَّ يَذُوقُونَ}: There are several views concerning it. The first: that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), informing about them with that. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لابثين», i.e. tarrying, not tasting; so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). The third: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أحقاب». Makkī said: "It bears the pronoun [latently] because it is a verb, so making it overt is not obligatory, even though it is an adjective applied to something other than the one to whom it belongs. It is only permissible for it to be an adjective of «أحقاب» because of the pronoun referring to al-aḥqāb in «فيها». If in the position of «يَذُوقون» there were an active participle, it would have been necessary to make the pronoun overt if you made it an adjective of «أحقاب»." The fourth: that it is an explanation of His saying «أحقاباً» if you make it accusative as a ḥāl with the interpretation mentioned earlier from al-Zamakhsharī, for he said: "And His saying «لا يَذوقون فيها بَرْداً ولا شَراباً» is an explanation of it." The fifth: that it is another ḥāl from «للطَّاغين», like «لابِثين».

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ حَمِيماً}: It may be a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) from His saying «شَراباً», and this is clear. The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means: they do not taste in it any coolness or refreshment that relieves them from the heat of the Fire, nor any drink that calms their thirst, but they taste in it scalding water and pus."
I say: Makkī, when he made it disconnected, took «البَرْد» to denote sleep; he said: "If you make it sleep, then «حميماً» is an exception that is not of the [genus of the] first." What led al-Zamakhsharī to [hold it] disconnected, despite the term "drink" truly applying to scalding water and pus, was his description of it with his saying "nor any drink that calms their thirst"; with this restriction the scalding water is not of the genus of this drink. Applying «البَرْد» to sleep is the dialect of Hudhayl, and [the poet] recited:
4470 - فإن شِئْتِ حَرَّمْتُ النِّساءَ سواكمُ ... وإنْ شِئْتِ لم أَطْعَمْ نُقاخاً ولا بَرْداً
(If you wish, I will forbid myself all women but you; and if you wish, I will taste neither fresh water nor sleep.)
In the speech of one of the Bedouins: "The cold (al-bard) prevented sleep (al-bard)". It was said: it was named so because it cuts off the violence of thirst. Tasting, on these two views—I mean its being a refreshment relieving them from the heat, and its being sleep—is figurative. As for the view of those who make it a name for cool, pleasant drink—it is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he recited the saying of Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him:
4471 - يَسْقُونَ مْن وَرَدَ البَرِيصَ عليهمُ ... بَرْداً يُصَفِّقُ بالرَّحيقِ السَّلْسَلِ
(They give whoever comes down to al-Barīṣ to them cool water mixed with smooth-flowing pure wine.)
and the saying of the other:
4472 - أَمانِيُّ مِنْ سُعْدَى حِسانٌ كأنَّما ... سَقَتكَ بها سُعْدى على ظَمَأ بَرْدا
(Fair hopes from Suʿdā, as if with them Suʿdā gave you cool water to drink in thirst.)
—then the tasting is literal, except that there then becomes a repetition with His saying after that «ولا شراباً».
The third: that it is a badal (substitute) for His saying «ولا شراباً», and this is the best, because the speech is not affirmative. The readers' disagreement over {وَغَسَّاقاً}, with and without doubling, has preceded, along with the discussion of it and of «حميم».

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {جَزَآءً}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Its governing word is either his saying «لا يذوقون» to its end, because it is equivalent to "they were recompensed with that", or an omitted verb. «وِفاقاً» is an adjective of it by way of exaggeration, or with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "possessing conformity". Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with shadda on the fāʾ, from waffaqahu li-kadhā.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {كِذَّاباً}: the majority read kiddhāban with shadda on the dhāl. By right the maṣdar of faʿʿala ought to come on the pattern of taf ʿīl, like ṣarrafa taṣrīfan. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pattern fiʿʿāl in the whole of the chapter of faʿʿala is widespread in the speech of eloquent Arabs, who say nothing else. One of them heard me explaining a verse and said: 'You have explained it with a fissār the like of which was never heard.' Another said: it is the dialect of some Arabs, the Yemenis, and he cited: 4473 - لقد طالَ ما ثَبَّطْتَني عن صَحابتي ... وعن حاجةٍ قِضَّاؤُها مِنْ شِفائِيا (You have long held me back from my companions and from a need whose fulfilment is my cure.) He means: taqaḍḍīhā. The base form is on taf ʿīl, and it is like zakkā tazkiya. One of them was heard asking for a legal ruling about his pilgrimage and said: 'Is al-ḥalq dearer to you or al-qiṣṣār?' meaning al-taqṣīr (shortening)."
ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Aʿmash, Abū Rajāʾ and ʿĪsā of Basra read it with light pronunciation. It is a maṣdar, either of this overt verb by omission of the augments, or of an implied verb, like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is like his saying {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً}, meaning: they denied Our signs, so they lied a lying; or you make it accusative by «كَذَّبوا» because it includes the meaning of kadhabū, since everyone who denies the truth is a liar. If you make it in the sense of mukādhaba, its meaning is: they denied Our signs and so contended in lying a contending; or they denied them as contenders in lying, because they are liars in the view of the Muslims and the Muslims are liars in their view, so there is mukādhaba between them; or because they speak with extreme exaggeration in lying, the action of one who strives to prevail in a matter and so exerts his utmost effort." Abū al-Faḍl said: "That is a dialect of the Yemenis, in that they make the maṣdar of kadhaba lightened, kidhāban, with light pronunciation, like kataba kitāban, so that the maṣdar here is of the meaning of the verb and not of its form, like aʿṭaytuhu ʿaṭāʾan." I say: as for kadhaba kidhāban with light pronunciation in both, it is well known, and from it is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
4474 - فَصَدَقْتُها وكَذَبْتُها ... والمَرْءُ يَنْفَعُه كِذابُه
(I told her the truth and I lied to her; and a man may benefit from his lying.)
ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and al-Mājishūn read «كُذَّاباً» with ḍamma on the kāf and shadda on the dhāl. It has two explanations. The first is that it is the plural of kādhib, like ḍurrāb for ḍārib. On this it is accusative as a confirming ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), that is: they denied while being liars. The second is that kudhdhāb is a singular meaning one extreme in lying. One says: rajulun kudhdhāb, like your saying "ḥussān", so it is made a description of the maṣdar of kadhdhabū, that is: a denial that is kudhdhāb, extreme in its lying. Al-Zamakhsharī said both.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ}: the majority read it in the accusative, by the construction of preoccupation (ishtighāl), and this is the preferred view because a verbal clause precedes. Abū al-Sammāl read it in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as the khabar (predicate). This clause is parenthetical (muʿtaraḍ) between the cause and the effect, because the original is: "they denied Our signs with a denial, so taste." His saying «فذوقوا» is a consequence of their denial.
His saying: {كِتَاباً}: there are several views on it. First, that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of «أَحْصَيْنا», that is, iḥṣāʾan; the figurative usage is then in the maṣdar itself. Second, that it is a maṣdar for «أَحْصَيْنا» because it has the meaning of "We wrote"; the figurative usage is then in the verb itself. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "because counting and writing meet in the meaning of recording and tallying." Third, that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) meaning: written in the Tablet.

semin-durr:32-32.t: His saying: {حَدَآئِقَ}: it may be a badal (substitute) from «مَفازاً», a badal al-ishtimāl, or a badal kull min kull (total substitute) by way of exaggeration, in that these very things are made the place of success. It may also be accusative by an omitted «aʿnī» ("I mean"). It is also said that «مَفازاً» has the meaning of al-fawz (success), so a muḍāf is implied, that is: the success of gardens.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {وَكَوَاعِبَ}: kawāʿib is the plural of kāʿib, which is a girl whose breast has become rounded, that is, has become round. He said:
4475 - وكان مِجَنِّي دونَ مَنْ كَنْتُ أتَّقي ... ثلاثُ شُخوصٍ كاعِبانِ ومُعْصِرُ
(My shield against those I was guarding against were three figures, two budding girls and one nearing maturity.)
Qays ibn ʿĀṣim al-Minqarī said:
4476 - وكم مِنْ حَصانٍ قد حَوَيْنا كَريمةٍ ... ومِنْ كاعبٍ لم تَدْرِما البؤسُ مُعْصِرِ
(How many a chaste, noble woman have we taken, and how many a budding girl nearing maturity who did not know what hardship is.)
The atrāb (peers) have been mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {دِهَاقاً}: an adjective of «كأس». Al-dihāq means full, brimming. It is said to be taken from dahaqahu, that is, he pressed it and tightened it with his hand, as if he filled the hand and it was compressed. The poet said:
4477 - لأَنْتِ إلى الفؤادِ أحَبُّ قُرْباً ... من الصَّادي إلى الكأسِ الدهاق
(You are dearer to the heart in nearness than the cup brimming full is to one parched with thirst.)
/ It is also said: al-dihāq means successive. It was cited:
4478 - أتانا عامِرٌ يَبْغي قِراناً ... فأتْرَعْنا له كأساً دِهاقا
(ʿĀmir came to us seeking companionship, so we filled for him a brimming cup.)

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {وَلاَ كِذَّاباً}: al-Kisāʾī reads it with light pronunciation, and the others with heavy. Al-Kisāʾī agreed with the group in the first only because of the explicit mention of its verb with shadda, which requires that «كِذّاباً» not be lightened. This is what was mentioned earlier in his saying {فَتُفَجِّرَ الأنهار} [al-Isrāʾ: 91], where there was no disagreement, because its verb is explicitly stated with it, unlike the first. Makkī said: "Whoever pronounced it with shadda made it the maṣdar of «كَذَّبَ», with an alif added to it as it is added in «إكراماً»; and their saying «تَكْذيباً»: they made the tāʾ a replacement for the doubling of the ʿayn, and the yāʾ in place of the alif, changing its beginning as they changed its end. The base form of the maṣdar of the quadriliteral is that it comes to the number of letters of the past tense with an added alif, with a change of vowels. They said «تَكَلُّماً», so the maṣdar came to the number of letters of the past tense without an added alif because of the number of its letters; the lām was given ḍamma and not kasra, because it is not a noun on the pattern tafaʿʿil, and was not given fatḥa so that it would not be confused with the past tense." The reading of al-Kisāʾī «كِذاباً» with light pronunciation made it the maṣdar of kadhdhaba kidhāban. It is also said: it is the maṣdar of «كَذَب», like your saying kataba kitāban.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {جَزَآءً}: a confirming maṣdar (maṣdar muʾakkid), accusative, with the meaning: "for the God-fearing there is success", as if it were said: He recompensed the God-fearing with success.
His saying «عَطاءً» is a badal (substitute) from «جَزاءً», and it is an ism maṣdar (noun of the verbal noun). He said:
4479 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وبعدَ عَطائِك المِئةَ الرِّتاعا
(... and after your gift of the hundred grazing camels.)
Al-Zamakhsharī made it accusative by «جزاءً» as the accusative of a direct object. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected this, saying that he made «جزاءً» a confirming maṣdar of the content of the sentence «إنَّ للمتقين [مفازاً]». He said: "The confirming maṣdar does not govern, because it cannot be resolved into a maṣdar particle and a verb, and we know of no disagreement about this."
His saying: {حِسَاباً}: an adjective of «عطاءً», the meaning being "sufficient", so it is a maṣdar put in the place of the adjective, or exaggeration is intended in it, or there is an omitted muḍāf, from their saying aḥsabanī al-shayʾ, that is, it sufficed me. Abū al-Barhasam and Shurayḥ ibn Yazīd al-Ḥimṣī read it with shadda on the sīn while the ḥāʾ keeps its kasra. Its analysis is that it is a maṣdar like kiddhāb, put in the place of the adjective, that is: a gift that is muḥsib, that is, sufficient. Ibn Quṭayb read likewise except that he gave the ḥāʾ fatḥa. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "He built faʿʿāl from afʿala, like darrāk from adraka", meaning that it is an intensive adjective, from aḥsaba in the sense of "sufficed such-and-such". Ibn ʿAbbās read «حَسَنَا» with nūn, from al-ḥusn (goodness). Sirāj read «حَسْباً» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the sīn and the single-dotted bāʾ, that is, a sufficient gift, from your saying ḥasbuka kadhā, that is, it suffices you.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {رَّبِّ السماوات}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «ربُّ السماواتِ» and «الرحمنُ» in the nominative. Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read both in the genitive, and the two (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read the first in the genitive and the second in the nominative. As for reading both in the nominative, it is permissible in several ways. The first: that «ربُّ» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "He is the Lord", and «الرحمنُ» likewise, or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «لا يَمْلِكون». The second: that «ربُّ» is made the mubtadaʾ and «الرحمنُ» its khabar, with «لا يَمْلِكون» a second khabar or resumptive. The third: that «ربُّ» is also a mubtadaʾ and «الرحمنُ» its naʿt (adjective), with «لا يَمْلِكون» the khabar of «رَبُّ». The fourth: that «رَبُّ» is a mubtadaʾ, «الرحمنُ» a second mubtadaʾ, and «لا يَمْلِكون» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of the first. The link is achieved by repeating the mubtadaʾ in its meaning, and this is the opinion of al-Akhfash. It is also possible that «لا يَمْلكون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), an inseparable one.
As for reading both in the genitive, it is as a badal (substitute), or bayān (explication), or naʿt (adjective), both to the first, except that repeating the badal is open to consideration, and I drew attention to that near the end of this topic, at the end of al-Fātiḥa; or «ربِّ السماواتِ» is made to follow the first and «الرحمن» to follow the second, as mentioned earlier. As for the genitive of the first, it is by following the first, and the nominative of the second is as a mubtadaʾ, with the verbal clause as khabar, or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and «لا يَمْلِكون» is as mentioned before: resumptive, or second khabar, or inseparable ḥāl.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَقُومُ}: accusative, either by «لا يتكلَّمون» which follows it, or by «لا يَمْلِكون». «صَفَّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, standing in ranks. «لا يتكلَّمون» is either a ḥāl or resumptive.
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ}: it may be a badal (substitute) from the wāw of «يتكلمون», and this is the preferred view because the sentence is not affirmative, or it may be accusative on the basis of the original rule of exception.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ}: it may be / a badal (substitute) from «يَومَ» before it, or accusative by «عذاباً», that is: the punishment will occur on that day. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be an adjective of «قريباً»; had he made it an adjective of «عذاباً» it would have been better. The majority read «المَرْءُ» with fatḥa on the mīm, which is the higher form. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with ḍamma, which is a dialect: they make the fāʾ follow the lām. Abū Ḥātim called this reading wrong, but he is not correct, since it is established as a dialect.
His saying: {مَا قَدَّمَتْ}: it may be interrogative, suspending «يَنْظُرُ» (ʿalliqa) if it is from al-naẓar (looking), in which case the clause is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition; or it may be a relative noun functioning as the object, with al-naẓar meaning waiting, that is: he waits for what his hands have sent forward. The majority do not assimilate the tāʾ of «كنتُ» into «تُراباً»; they said: because the agent is not omitted, and assimilation resembles omission. In his saying «ويقولُ الكافرُ» an overt noun is placed where a pronoun would be expected, as testimony against him to that effect.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (١) عَنِ النَّبَأِ الْعَظِيمِ (٢) الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ (٣)).
We have already discussed the dropping of the alif of «مَا» in the interrogative.
(عَنْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَتَسَاءَلُونَ». As for the second «عَنْ», it is a badal (substitute) for the first, and the interrogative alif, which ought to be repeated, is omitted; or it is attached to another verb, not one being asked about, i.e. «يَتَسَاءَلُونَ عَنِ النَّبَأِ» (they ask one another about the news). (الَّذِي) admits the genitive, the accusative and the nominative.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا (٨)).
(أَزْوَاجًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. of one kind, resembling one another.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا (١٦)).
The words of the Exalted (أَلْفَافًا): it is the plural of «لِفّ», like «جِذْع» and «أَجْذَاع». It is also said that it is the plural of «لُفّ», and «لُفّ» is the plural of «لَفَّاء» (dense).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا (١٨)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ): it is a badal (substitute) for «يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ» or for «مِيقَاتًا», or it is accusative by the implied verb «أَعْنِي» (I mean).
(أَفْوَاجًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:21-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا (٢١) لِلطَّاغِينَ مَآبًا (٢٢) لَابِثِينَ فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا (٢٣) لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًا وَلَا شَرَابًا (٢٤) إِلَّا حَمِيمًا وَغَسَّاقًا (٢٥) جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا (٢٦)).
The words of the Exalted (لِلطَّاغِينَ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَآبًا», i.e. a place of return for the transgressors; or a naʿt (adjective) of «مِرْصَادًا»; or the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مِرْصَادًا» itself.
(لَابِثِينَ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «الطَّاغِينَ» — an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).
(أَحْقَابًا) is governed by «لَابِثِينَ». It is also said that it is governed by «لَا يَذُوقُونَ», and that by «أَحْقَابًا» here eternity is meant. «لَا يَذُوقُونَ» is another ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لَابِثِينَ».
(جَزَاءً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. they were recompensed with that by way of recompense.

ukberi-tibyan:28-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّابًا (٢٨) وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَابًا (٢٩)).
(كِذَّابًا) with doubling is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «التَّكْذِيب» (denial); and without doubling (كِذَابًا) it is the maṣdar of «كَذَبَ» when lying is repeated by him, and in meaning it is close to «كَذَبَ». (وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ) is accusative by an omitted verb. (كِتَابًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. written; and it may be a maṣdar according to the meaning, because «أَحْصَيْنَاهُ» means «كَتَبْنَاهُ» (We recorded it).

ukberi-tibyan:31-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا (٣١) حَدَائِقَ وَأَعْنَابًا (٣٢) وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَابًا (٣٣) وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا (٣٤) لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا وَلَا كِذَّابًا (٣٥)). (حَدَائِقَ) is a badal (substitute) for «مَفَازًا».
(لَا يَسْمَعُونَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ», and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:36-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَزَاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ عَطَاءً حِسَابًا (٣٦) رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الرَّحْمَنِ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَابًا (٣٧)).
(عَطَاءً) is a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), and it is a badal (substitute) for «جَزَاءً».
(رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ) in the nominative (رَبُّ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on its khabar (predicate):
First: «الرَّحْمَنُ», in which case what follows it is another khabar, or resumptive.
Second: «الرَّحْمَنُ» is a naʿt (adjective), and «لَا يَمْلِكُونَ» is the khabar.
«رَبُّ» may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هُوَ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ» (He is the Lord of the heavens), with «الرَّحْمَنُ» and what follows it as a mubtadaʾ and khabar. «رَبِّ» and «الرَّحْمَنِ» are also read in the genitive as a badal for «رَبِّكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ صَفًّا لَا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ. . .)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ يَقُومُ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for «لَا يَمْلِكُونَ», for «خِطَابًا», or for «لَا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ». «صَفًّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَنْذَرْنَاكُمْ عَذَابًا قَرِيبًا يَوْمَ يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ. . . (٤٠)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ يَنْظُرُ): i.e. the punishment of a day, so it is a badal (substitute).
It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «قَرِيبًا». And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Nabaʾ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾: its origin is «عَنْ ما يَتَساءَلُونَ؟!»; the nūn was assimilated into the mīm because the mīm shares with the nūn the nasal resonance (ghunna). We have explained earlier in the book why the alif was dropped. The meaning is: "About what thing are they asking one another?!" The wording is that of a question, but the meaning is to magnify the matter, as you say «أيُّ شَيْءٍ زَيْدٌ» ("what a thing Zayd is!"). Then He made it clear, saying: ﴿عَنِ النَّبَإ العَظِيمِ﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 2]. It was said that it is the Qur'an; it was said: about the resurrection; and it was said: about the matter of the Prophet ﷺ. What indicates it is His saying ﴿إنَّ يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ كانَ مِيقاتًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 17], which indicates that they were asking one another about the resurrection.
