zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — it was also read «كَلّا سَتَعْلَمُونَ» with tāʾ. What the readers follow is «كَلّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ» with yāʾ, and it is better; the tāʾ is transmitted from al-Ḥasan.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿ألَمْ نَجْعَلِ الأرْضَ مِهادًا﴾ — it was also read «مَهْدًا», but most readers read it ﴿مِهادًا﴾, and the meaning is the same. Its interpretation is: We made it submissive for them so that they dwell on it and travel through its tracts.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَخَلَقْناكم أزْواجًا﴾: He created the male and the female. It was also said: «أزْواجًا», that is: kinds.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا نَوْمَكم سُباتًا﴾: «اَلسُّباتُ» is that one is cut off from movement while the spirit is in his body; that is: We made your sleep a rest for you.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا اللَّيْلَ لِباسًا﴾, that is: you find repose in it, and it wraps around you.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَبَنَيْنا فَوْقَكم سَبْعًا شِدادًا﴾, that is: seven heavens.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا سِراجًا وهّاجًا﴾, that is: We placed the sun in them as a lamp. The interpretation of ﴿وَهّاجًا﴾ is: blazing.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا مِنَ المُعْصِراتِ ماءً ثَجّاجًا﴾: «اَلْمُعْصِراتُ» are the clouds, because they press out (taʿṣir) the water. It was also said: «اَلْمُعْصِراتُ» is as one says «قَدْ أُجِزَّ الزَّرْعُ، فَهو مُجَزٌّ» ("the crop is ripe for cutting") — when it reaches the point of being rained from, it has «أعْصَرَ». The meaning of «ثَجّاجٌ» is: pouring.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا ونَباتًا﴾: everything that is harvested is grain (ḥabb), and every pasture that livestock eat is vegetation (nabāt).

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿وَجَنّاتٍ ألْفافًا﴾, that is: and gardens with intertwined trees. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known what He created and that He is able to resurrect, and said: ﴿إنَّ يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ كانَ مِيقاتًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 17].

zajjaj:18-18.t:
﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ﴾ is a badal (substitute) from «يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ»; if you wish, it is an explanation of «يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ». We have explained «اَلصُّورُ» earlier. ﴿فَتَأْتُونَ أفْواجًا﴾, that is: every community comes with its leader.
﴿وَفُتِحَتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ أبْوابًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 19], that is: it is split open, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 1], ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 1].

zajjaj:21-22.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كانَتْ مِرْصادًا﴾ ﴿لِلطّاغِينَ مَآبًا﴾, that is: it lies in wait for the people of unbelief and for whoever has deserved the punishment; it almost bursts with rage, and none upon whom the word of punishment has been realised passes beyond it. The meaning of ﴿مَآبًا﴾ is: to it they are returned.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿لابِثِينَ فِيها أحْقابًا﴾, and «لَبِثِينَ» (also read): one says «لَبِثَ الرَّجُلُ، فَهو لابِثٌ» ("the man stayed, so he is staying"), and one says «هُوَ لُبْثٌ بِمَكانِ كَذا», that is: staying has become his habit. «اَلْأحْقابُ», its singular is «حُقْبٌ», and «اَلْحُقْبُ» is eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, and each day equal in length to a thousand years of the years of this world. The meaning is that they remain for ages, not tasting during those ages any coolness or drink, while they abide in the Fire forever, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: «خالِدِينَ فِيها أبَدًا».

zajjaj:24-24.t: The meaning of ﴿لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْدًا﴾: it was said: sleep. And it may be: "they taste therein no coolness of wind, nor of shade, nor of sleep."

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿إلا حَمِيمًا وغَسّاقًا﴾, that is: they taste nothing therein except boiling water (ḥamīm), which is at the extreme of heat.
As for «اَلْغَسّاقُ», it was said: what oozes (yaghsiq) from their skins, that is, flows. And it was said: «اَلْغَسّاقُ» is what is intensely cold.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿جَزاءً وِفاقًا﴾, that is: they were requited in accordance with their deeds.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿إنَّهم كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ حِسابًا﴾, that is: they do not believe in the resurrection, nor that they will be brought to account and hope for the reward of a reckoning.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كِذّابًا﴾: this is the majority reading. It was also read «كِذابًا» without doubling. ﴿كِذّابًا﴾ with doubling is more frequent, and among the maṣdars (verbal nouns) of the pattern «فَعَّلْتُ» it is better than «فِعالٌ». The poet said:
؎لَقَدْ طالَ ما رَيَّثَتْنِي عَنْ صَحابَتِي ∗∗∗ وعَنْ حِوَجٍ قَضّاؤُها مِن شِفائِيا
(Long indeed has she held me back from my companions, and from needs whose fulfilment would be my cure.)
— from «قَضَيْتُ قَضاءً». And like «كِذابًا» without doubling is the saying of the poet:
؎فَصَدَقْتُها وكَذَّبْتُها ∗∗∗ والمَرْءُ يَنْفَعُهُ كِذابُهْ
(I told her the truth and I lied to her, and a man may profit from his lying.)

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أحْصَيْناهُ كِتابًا﴾: «وَكُلَّ» is accusative through an implied (muḍmar) verb which «أحْصَيْناهُ كِتابًا» explains; the meaning is: "and We have enumerated everything — We have enumerated it."
His saying ﴿كِتابًا﴾ is tawkīd (emphasis) of His saying «أحْصَيْناهُ», because the meaning of «أحْصَيْناهُ» and «كَتَبْناهُ», as regards what is obtained and established, is one; so the meaning is: "We wrote it down in writing."

zajjaj:34-34.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَكَأْسًا دِهاقًا﴾, that is: the implied structure of the verse is "they did not hope for the reward of a reckoning", so there is an omitted muḍāf there.
«[Translator's note: this sentence on the omitted muḍāf concerns verse 27 (﴿لا يَرْجُونَ حِسابًا﴾), not verse 34; it is translated where the source places it.]»
Abū Isḥāq said: "Al-kaʾs: every vessel containing drink is a kaʾs, and if there is no drink in it, it is not a kaʾs. Likewise al-māʾida: whatever table has food upon it is a māʾida." The meaning of «دِهاقًا» is: full. It has also come in the exegesis that it is pure. The poet said:
؎يَلَذُّهُ بِكَأْسِهِ الدِّهاقُ
(He relishes it in his brimming cup.)

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿جَزاءً مِن رَبِّكَ عَطاءً حِسابًا﴾: it is accusative through the meaning of «إنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفازًا»; the meaning is: "He requited them with that as a requital." Likewise ﴿عَطاءً حِسابًا﴾, because the meaning of «أعْطاهُمْ» and «جَزاهُمْ» is one. «حِسابًا» means: what suffices them, that is: in it is what they desire. One says «أحْسَبَنِي كَذا وكَذا» in the sense of: it sufficed me.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿رَبِّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: it was read in the genitive as an attribute, following His saying «مِن رَبِّكَ رَبِّ», and it was read «رَبُّ» in the sense "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth". Likewise «اَلرَّحْمَنُ» ﴿لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنهُ خِطابًا﴾ was read in the genitive and the nominative, and its explanation is the explanation of «رَبِّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ».

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ والمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا﴾: «اَلرُّوحُ» is a creation like humans, but it is not human. It was also said: «اَلرُّوحُ» is Jibrīl, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَن شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إلى رَبِّهِ مَآبًا﴾, that is: a place of return.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرابًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that on the Day of Resurrection retaliation will be taken for the hornless animal (al-jammāʾ) from the horned one — «اَلْجَمّاءُ» is the one that has no horn — then Allah the Exalted will make them all dust, and that dust is the darkness (al-qatara) that covers the faces of the unbelievers and rises over their faces; so the unbeliever wishes that he were dust. It has also been said that the meaning of ﴿يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرابًا﴾ is: would that I had not been resurrected, as He said: ﴿يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 25].
